title: The Royal Hotel
excerpt:
Battered fish, chips, and salad
Cheeseburger and chips

What a surprise. Yes, this establishment is a bit run down and the menu is basic. But the food was well made, tasty, and excellent value for money. Exceeded expectations. In particular the salad with the fish & chips - many places just phone this salad in. Not The Royal. Fancy lettuce, red onion, carrot, cheese, capsicum, tomato, cucumber, salad dressing. Not two sad lettuce leaves and a single slice of cucumber like you get in some pubs. Also they weren’t shy with the tartare and tomato sauces. And they had chicken salt on the chips for both meals, plus the burger was huge. If you want to enter the pool comp, be sure to bring your own cue. It’s pretty serious business.

title: The Cooperage Cafe
excerpt:
Chicken, cranberry, and cream cheese filo with salad
Butter chicken pie with salad
Carrot cake with yoghurt
Banana smoothie

Oh dear, everything went wrong here. Although we weren’t planning on drinking anything alcoholic, this establishment loudly announces on its signage that it is a licensed cafe. Right inside the door however is a sign that says no alcohol, and this is honestly the least of their problems. There was a really long and slow queue to order, and when we did finally order two items from their menu, we were informed that the wait would be 40 minutes. That’s understandable on an exceptionally busy day, but The Cooperage was only about a third full… we just ate from the cabinet. The filo, the pie, and the carrot cake were passable. The salads that came with the meals had too much dressing, too much carrot, and not a lot of anything else. There was something wrong with the yoghurt, in fact, it was inedible. Two mysterious bowls, one of sour cream and one of tomato relish were delivered, it was not exactly clear what they were supposed to accompany, so we tried them both with everything hot. That was a mistake. The smoothie was from one of those Zero Degrees powder sachets, nobody would think there was any banana involved, and there was an unpleasant aftertaste typical of these powder smoothies. The staff seemed very stressed, and on the whole, not pleased to be there. There appear to be some management issues at The Cooperage, the last time we tried to eat here we were told we could only order from the cabinet as there was no cook. The whole experience was a bummer.

title: O'Briens Irish sandwich Cafe
excerpt:
Celtic: mixed leaves, sundried tomato, cheddar, and red onion on multigrain bread
Breakfast bun: bacon, egg, sausage and hollandaise on ciabatta
Banana smoothie
Peanut butter slab

O’Briens makes a killer sandwich. The Celtic, which we asked to have without avocado, was very nice. Red onion is always a risk in a sandwich, often you get colossal pieces that all come out the side at once, in the Celtic however, the red onion was very subtle, and well proportioned. The ciabatta of the breakfast bun, was outstanding, soft, toasted to perfection, and delicious, but there were some minor structural issues. Both sandwiches came with ready salted chips, which was unusual, but not unwelcome. The banana smoothie certainly wasn’t bad, but it didn’t turn any heads. And the peanut butter slab was like a big Reese’s piece, and what’s not to like about that. It looks like a 90’s Robert Harris on the inside, could use a revamp. The menu was vast and varied, truly a sandwich for every taste.

title: Moxie's Cafe
excerpt:
Eggs benedict with mushroom
Pork belly burger with chips

Let us tell you about Steve’s latte. Moxies was quite busy when we arrived, with a few reserved tables. The table next to us was reserved for Steve. While we were waiting for our meals to come out (which took 20 minutes, but they had told us 30 minutes and to be fair it was fairly busy) we watched with interest as a latte bowl complete with chocolate fish was delivered to Steve’s reserved empty table for two. The latte sat there. And sat there. At a time when the latte was surely lukewarm the apparent manager (judging by the way he was bustling about and shaking hands with customers) removed the latte from the table and moved it to a neighbouring, non-reserved and much larger table. He removed the saucer and placed it atop the bowl as a lid of sorts, assumedly in a vain attempt to keep what little heat remained inside. Some time later a man and a woman arrived and sat at Steve’s table. Was this Steve? Less than one minute later their meals arrived - Steve (?) and associate had clearly ordered in advance. Yet the latte remained banished to the other table. More mysteriously still, shortly after this two coffees (none of which was a latte bowl) arrived for Steve (?) and associate. Just as we were ready to give up hope, a gentleman arrived at the latte table. The manager greeted him and indicated the latte bowl, which the man started to drink. Was THIS Steve? Then who had sat at Steve’s table? And why was the latte prepared SO FAR IN ADVANCE of either Steves’ arrivals? We left Moxies after a pretty average meal with more questions than answers.

During this drama, we did receive our food. The eggs benedict was just like a thousand others we’ve had. The pork belly burger was comically over-tall and so impossible to eat without deconstruction. Even if the burger hadn’t been taller than Business Andy’s face, pork belly is not suitable as a burger filling as it is too chewy - pulled pork would have been preferable. The burger was nice, just difficult to eat.

title: Shake Out
excerpt:
Cheeseburger
Chicken burger
Cheesy fries
Cheesecake shake

Shake Out is a fast food burger establishment, with a difference. The set-up is designed to be streamlined with cashierless, cashless ordering using a tablet, a limited menu and no customisation. Speaking as people who sometimes like to remove the tomato from their burger, the lack of customisation was a little disappointing. However, the burgers were very good. Quality, fresh ingredients and great buns, these were simple burgers done well. The burgers are small which is great for lunch and was reflected in the price. The cheesy fries came with a cheese dipping sauce which was a bit heart attack-esque. The cheesecake shake was similarly artery clogging but we appreciated the unique cheesecake flavour, although it was a bit sweet and was very thick - we recommend mixing the shake thoroughly before drinking.

excerpt:

The service in Angkor Wat was so excellent that, were there a rating for service alone, this would be at the top. The woman at the counter was an absolute delight - patient, friendly, laughed at all our jokes and even cracked one herself. Unfortunately, our rating system is not on service alone and the food at Angkor Wat was only so-so. Some care had been taken in constructing the burgers including fresh fancy lettuce and tomato. However, the fish was a little fishy and there was a bit too much lettuce in the fish burger. The satay chicken burger was a little better but still only okay.

A note on the clientele. In the average population, what proportion would you expect to have a limp? Five percent? Ten percent? Try seventy-five percent (of the customers dining in, excluding us). Seems a little extreme. Did something happen here?

title: Little India
excerpt:
Lamb pasanda with rice
Malai kofta with rice
Plain naan
Paneer kulcha

It’s not easy for a chain Indian restaurant to distinguish itself. We’ve all had countless middle-of-the-road curries, each a duplicate of the one before. Maybe occasionally you’ll branch out, try something new, only to be struck down with immediate regret and go crawling back to your boring korma. Not at Little India. Both curries were absolutely delicious, in particular the malai kofta was the best curry either of us has had in some years. Naans were piping hot, and the rice was fluffy and plentiful. We do have a few minor issues to point out. The water jug was apparently made of lead, or possibly the collapsed innards of a black hole, it was much too heavy. The service was patchy, on the one hand they were very attentive… so attentive that they were in the way and couldn’t take a hint that a conversation was over. And on the other hand our stacked dirty dinner dishes sat on our table for an inordinate amount of time, in fact they were still there when we finally left. However none of this changes the fact that this was a scrumptious meal.

We do have a few minor issues to point out. The water jug was apparently made of lead, or possibly the collapsed innards of a black hole, it was much too heavy. The service was patchy, on the one hand they were very attentive… so attentive that they were in the way and couldn’t take a hint that a conversation was over. And on the other hand our stacked dirty dinner dishes sat on our table for an inordinate amount of time, in fact they were still there when we finally left. However none of this changes the fact that this was a scrumptious meal.
address: 157 Broadway Avenue, City Centre, Palmerston North 4410

Arranged Marriage is not a typical Indian Restaurant. Many of the familiar curries are absent, and replaced by exotic fare such as dosa, grilled fish in banana leaf, and cauliflower Manchurian. Of the mix platter starters the lentil doughnuts were the hero, while the dry fried beef could stay home if he wanted.

title: Tikka Talks
excerpt:
Poppadums with cumin seeds

Paneer tikka masala with rice
Beef jalfrezi with rice
Aloo paratha
Onion kulcha
A small thing of mint yoghurt sauce

Let me tell you who’s punching above their weight; Tikka Talks is punching above their weight. The place looks awful. We were the only people there and decorations included a pool table, seven empty food cabinets, a childrens’ play pen, a collection of four Warehouse-esque kiwi themed framed inspirational prints, and a large green dreamcatcher with a unicorn in the centre. But all this was saved by one man, and his mission, which was to upsell us at every opportunity, and to slay us with his jokes. Our original order was two curries, one plain naan, and one cheese naan, but the man drives a hard bargain, and by the time we realised that we had been worked by a skilled salesman, it was far too late. We were assured that we were going to be served something special that we were going to love, and he was right, dammit. The cumin seeds in the poppadums was a nice touch, the bhaji was just the way we like it, and the tamarind sauce, which we were proudly assured was made from scratch, was excellent. The curries themselves were both delicious. And as for the breads, the onion kulcha was sweet and tasty, while the aloo was just alright. Tikka Talks deserves more customers.

title: Cafe Express
excerpt:
Meatlovers pizza
Pesto pasta

If you like huge meals, Cafe Express is the place for you. If you like nice meals, maybe not so much. The “medium” pizza and “small” pasta we ordered would have comfortably fed three people, and for a very modest price. Unfortunately, the flavours couldn’t keep up with the value. The pasta was nice on the first bite. But two to three bites in it became apparent that this was really just spaghetti in a white sauce with minimal pesto and parmesan resulting in a bland dish. This became tedious very fast and was a long, long slog to the bottom of the bowl. The pizza was better than the pasta, but hardly turning heads. It was way over-cheesed. This resulted in serious structural issues as well as sogginess in the centre of the pizza. The meats themselves were fine, but the pizza could have done with a BBQ sauce or something to add a little pizzazz. Also, there was a cat tower near the kitchen. Tragically we never saw any cats.

title: The Coffee Club
excerpt:
Beef brisket burger with chips 
Vegan chicken salad
Banana and honey smoothie

You may be wondering why we are reviewing a chain such as The Coffee Club. In this particular instance, there are two reasons. Firstly, no one is safe from Business Andy and the Fee-Rex. We will review any establishment, as long as it is dine-in. Secondly, the site where this Coffee Club now stands used to house a different cafe from which the Fee-Rex was fired as a teenager, so this was a bit of a destination. Let’s start on a positive - the burger was actually very nice. While the brisket itself was slightly dry, this was more than masked by the ample sauce. On the meh side, the smoothie had unfortunately been made with an under-ripe banana, resulting in a stringy and dry aftertaste. Smoothie texture and coolness was good. The vegan chicken salad sucked. We know what you’re thinking, perhaps we brought this on ourselves for ordering a vegan chicken salad. After all, we’re not even vegan. However, we firmly believe that any diner, vegans included, should be able to have a tasty meal, which this salad was not. The “vegan chicken” was extraordinarily dry and liberally doused in a hot sauce from the underpants of satan himself. The rest of the salad was actually fine, but the sauce had pervaded all, and the “chicken” was too offensive to be redeemed.

title: Tongariro Lodge
excerpt:
John Dory on Israeli couscous with salsa
Lamb rump, roast root veggies with red wine jus

This fish was the worst meal we have had in a long time. Bearing in mind that this establishment is part of a fishing lodge, you’d think they would know how to make a tasty fish meal. So colour us shocked when, for forty dollars no less, we were served a tasteless, clammy lump of fish. The waiter said this was pan fried. Bull. Shit. The skin on the fish was so slimy there was no way it had been in a pan. More like boiled by the taste of things. The couscous and salsa were no help. They were flavourless so the whole thing just ended up tasting like the goo you scrape off a fish. Also, would it kill you to open a window? Upon entry the restaurant was stifling hot, and we found ourselves frantically opening windows to tempt in a breeze. It felt like they’d had a fire going in there all day. Saving Tongariro Lodge from the lowest possible rating was the surprisingly good lamb rump. It was moist, flavourful, well cooked, and the root vegetables were the perfect accompaniment.

If we were rating for atmosphere alone, Cloverlea Tavern would be a 4. Sensational karaoke, everyone knew everyone, there was a meat raffle going around, and we spotted the world’s most magnificent mullet crooning “Country Roads.” However, Business Andy & the Fee-Rex is a restaurant review blog, not a bar atmosphere review blog. The menu was bar snacks, but some effort had been made. There was a tasty seasoning on top and both tartare and tomato sauce on the side. The fish was just fish bites, but they were about as good as fish bites get. The shrimp and squid rings were good, however the mussels were a bit old. Maybe it was the karaoke, or maybe it was the mullet, in any case we were strongly reminded of our time at Castle 789. For the record, Cloverlea Tavern is better in every way.

title: Cafe Ignition
excerpt:
Macaroni cheese
Nachos
Banana smoothie

Cafe Ignition has a great view. Of the tarmac. This is the cafe at the Palmerston North airport. And you can tell they’re used to a captive clientele. The food was bland across the board. The smoothie was the highlight. The lowlight was the macaroni cheese. We saw the individually served bowls in the cabinet, with a garnish of two slices of tomato, a couple of spinach leaves and a sprinkling of red onion on top. When this was served to us, the garnish was steaming hot. They had clearly just chucked the whole thing in the microwave. How lazy is that?! Considering there were no flights for the next 3 hours and the place was nearly completely empty, they had plenty of time to remove the garnish prior to heating if they had cared enough to do so. Speaking of things they didn’t care to do, perhaps the staff could do less sitting-in-the-corner-doing-a-crossword-puzzle and more wiping of tables and chairs, which were crumb-fest 2021. If you do, for some reason, still want to go to this cafe, then a note on parking. Unless you want to pay exorbitant airport parking fees, you will need to park some ways away. And we recommend you do not pay for airport parking, as you will need all your money to pay the ripoff airport prices for your tasteless meal.

Fried chicken burger with chips and aioli
Swamp Juice hazy IPA

Another excellent meal at Brew Union. The garlic bread was something else, and much more of a pizza bread than a normal loaf. We were pleasantly surprised by the passionfruit sauce that came with the calamari, and the calamari itself was also delicious and not chewy at all. The fried chicken burger was superior in taste but inferior in structural integrity to the beef burger we had on the previous visit. The steak paled in comparison to the other meals but was still good. Last time we were here, we were remiss in not trying a beer. The Swamp Juice was fruity and hoppy - a good beer.

Fried chicken

Unfortunately the jackfruit was a bit underwhelming, and there was no discernable BBQ taste. The chicken was a bit too spicy, but because they were dusted with chilli some pieces were much spicier than others. The croquettes were great, and were really crunchy on the outside. The Fee-Rex doesn’t normally like pork belly, but these skewers were exceptional. They were sticky, sweet, and very juicy, frankly we could smash some more of them right now.

title: Der Metz
excerpt:
Deutsche platte (big ol’ platter of meats)
Jägerschnitzel (beef schnitzel with mushroom gravy)

The decor at Der Metz, like the meat, was plentiful, overwhelming, and excellent. The walls were covered in all sorts, but dominated by a giant portrait of Kaiser Wilhelm. The waitresses wore dirndls, and the beer came in 1L steins, making it look very German in there. The key indicator of quality for a schnitzel is the gristle content, and this schnitzel had very little gristle. There was one gristly mouthful in a schnitzel the size of Nebraska. The mash was a great accompaniment, and the mushroom gravy was delicious. Staring down the meat mountain aka Deutche platter, was a daunting prospect. This meal was meat, lots of it, and two kinds of sauerkraut, less of it. Sausages, roast pork, pork belly, all of it good, and the sauerkraut was a pleasant surprise. But the best part was the dumplings. While there are three vegetarian options on the menu, this place is clearly all about the meat. Top tip: get an extra serve of gravy on the side.

title: Federal Delicatessen
excerpt:
Griddle cake
Cinnamon scroll

Federal Delicatessen is cool. A lot of effort has been made to make this place look like an old New York Deli, and we felt several degrees cooler just sitting there. Likewise, the menu is very American, you can order bottomless tea and filter coffee, there’s pastrami everywhere, you can get pie by the slice, and there’s even a Reuben available. The breakfast menu is atypical, but this is a good thing. Reader, you may have noticed these Business Andy and the Fee-Rex don’t review a lot of breakfasts. We’re sick of eggs Benedict, and we’re sick of knowing exactly what else is going to be on the menu before we arrive, it’s always so pedestrian. The cinnamon scroll was very good, but unevenly heated, which was a shame. The griddle cake was fantastic, it came with crunchy nutty stuff, floofy cinnamon butter, a small amount of syrup (just the right amount) and some blueberry compote. All in all, the griddle cake was stupendous.

The salad was overdressed, but came with plenty of parmesan, however you couldn’t taste much of anything but dressing. And the rigatoni was very nice, with the right ratio of pasta to spring vegetables.
address: 309 Broadway, Newmarket Rooftop on Braodway, Westfield Newmarket, Auckland 1023

title: Orlando Country Club

BBQ melt

The BBQ melt was very meaty and hearty, and had plenty of sauce; a winning combo. On your arrival at Orlando Country Club, you’ll notice the large sign detailing the dress code. No stubbies, no singlets, no hoodies, and presumably no facial tats. Who do they think they are? This isn’t a real country club, it’s just a driving range and cafe. And by the way, we saw all of these rules violated while we were there.

Beef short rib ragu

We were very impressed by the chicken, anyone who can take kale and turn it into something that the Fee-Rex wants to scrape up every last morsel of is a genius in our books. The walnut provided an incredible texture contrast, and it wasn’t a miserable small meal, which can sometimes happen at places like this; this was an entire meal all by itself and no sides were required. title: Subway
excerpt:
Meatball sub on rye bread (non-toasted) with smoked cheese, spinach, cucumber, onion, carrot, capsicum, olives, garlic aioli, and pepper
Steak panini with mozzarella, spinach, onion, capsicum, honey mustard, and ranch dressing

When you order a steak panini at Subway, you’re not expecting eye fillet, but you’re also not expecting dry steak with a layer on top that we genuinely thought was mushroom, but on reflection, was probably fat. This panini was flavourless, and we know what you’re thinking, Subway is what you make it. However on this occasion, we used the Subway recommended salads and cheese, and got a very bland result. Our compliment for this panini is that it was piping hot, some cafes could learn a lesson from Subway here. Fortunately, the meatball sub was a bit better, but ultimately only reaches the level of “adequate.” Why would you eat at Subway when O’Briens Irish Sandwich Cafe exists?

title: 4Flames
excerpt:
Lamb madras with rice
Paneer lababdar with rice
Plain naan
Cheese & garlic naan

Hey 4Flames, turn down the damn air conditioning. You know there’s a real problem when you can hear people at other tables also complaining about being cold. We felt bad for the women who showed up wearing tiny skirts as we were leaving. Putting the enthusiastic temperature regulation aside, the curries were very nice and quite different. The lababdar was sweet and creamy, and the madras was coconutty. Unfortunately, the chunks of paneer and lamb were far too big, and the paneer was very dense. The lamb was good for curry-grade lamb, but it was still curry-grade lamb. The presentation of the curries was atypical, and we liked it. Gone were the typical cauldrons of curry sauce with submerged chunks and the plate for mixing. Instead it was like how you make a curry at home; all in a bowl. This was way better, with the opportunity to just add rice to your bowl and mix - voila! If you’re looking for a quick meal, we recommend avoiding Friday night dining as the takeaway side of the business was pumping and dine-in wait times suffered. Reservations are strongly recommended.

title: Trio Cafe
excerpt:
Creamy mushrooms on toast
Big breakfast: bacon, sausage, eggs, toast, hash browns, mushrooms
Banana smoothie

When we arrived at Trio Cafe, we were alone, and the waitress looked surprised to see us. The whole time we were there, we were alone. When we ordered, she had to look up all the prices, we suspected that we were their first customers ever.  We thought “this doesn’t look good.” When the smoothie arrived, and was really a banana milkshake with a banana blended in, unmixed banana syrup at the bottom, a swirl of canned whipped cream on the top, and a flimsy straw that was far too small we thought, “this really doesn’t look good.” But then the food arrived, and the whole thing turned around. The mushrooms on toast were outstanding, and that’s not an easy thing to say about mushrooms on toast which are often mundane. The bread was delicious sourdough. The mushrooms themselves were so flavourful, we don’t even know how they did it. They came with a game-changing smear of pesto and a little balsamic reduction on the side which left us wondering why we aren’t all eating our mushrooms this way. The big breakfast hadn’t phoned it in. Herbed focaccia for the toast, the steaky bacon: perfectly crisped, two hash browns, mushrooms (unfortunately, not the same as on the other plate), and a cheesy sausage they had innovated split down the middle and cooked as two separate halves that had curled deliciously. It was even decoratively garnished with balsamic reduction and julienne vegetables. Our only complaint was slightly underdone eggs, which were supposed to come “your way” as per the menu, except they never asked and just came fried.

title: Ashhurst Inn
excerpt:
Man burger with chips
Fish, chips, and salad

The Ashhurst Inn has a very special place in our hearts. As Ashhurst residents, we are keen to support what is literally the only dine-in dinner establishment in the whole village, plus the Inn was the site of a very early date for Business Andy and The Fee-Rex. It pains us to say that this meal was bad, but it was bad, especially the burger. In fact, the man burger was tragic, it looked like the kind of disappointing burger that you make at home. While you’re making it, you’re so certain that it’s going to be great, but then you realise that the patty is so dry that it’s crumbling, the bun has been toasted way too long, there’s not nearly enough sauce, the cheese isn’t melted, you haven’t put enough bacon in it, and the hash brown doesn’t save it. The fish and chips wasn’t as bad as the burger, with both key components being passable. The salad, however, was a disgrace. Every ingredient was flavourless and tossed in a gross oily sauce. Shout out to the homemade tartare sauce, although it’s sad when the best part of two meals is tartare sauce.

title: Local
excerpt:
Poached egg on ciabatta with haloumi and potato hash
Scrambled eggs on multigrain with mushrooms, sausage, and black pudding
Golden milk latte

We really appreciated Local’s build your own breakfasts, which start with eggs on toast and become as much or as little as you want. We both went for this option, but ended up with fairly different breakfasts. The sausage was really nice, as were the black pudding and the haloumi. The toast and the mushroom were fine, and the potato hash was a bit too dry and a bit too crisp. The eggs were all perfectly cooked but what stood out was that the poached egg was 100% dry. We hate it when someone drops a poached egg onto your toast that’s still sopping wet from the pan, it ruins the toast. Plenty of breakfast joints do this, but not Local. The golden milk latte was unusual but nice. It doesn’t contain any coffee and was instead made with milk tumeric, cinnamon, date puree, and black pepper.

title: Burger King
excerpt:
Rodeo burger regular combo with a banana shake
Streaky bacon steakhouse regular combo with L&P

We knew we were off to a bad start when we arrived and saw seven (7!) people waiting for their food. Some of them probably had their food already, but had frozen solid and were unable to leave. We can only assume The King turns the temperature down that low to discourage youths from loitering in his fine establishment on a Friday night. Although they asked if we would be dining in at their wobbly, sticky tables, they still just gave us our meal in a takeaway bag anyway, making us feel even more unwelcome. To make matters worse, the food was awful. If the Burger King was alive to eat these burgers, he would have rolled over in his grave. For both burgers, the sauce did a lot of heavy lifting, attempting to moisten each mouthful and also disguise the other flavours. The rodeo burger was a little better than the streaky bacon steakhouse, which was a bit sad considering that the steakhouse burger is supposed to be from their premium range. It was anything but. The bun was stale, the distribution of ingredients was patchy, and when you got a taste of the meat without sauce, you wished that you hadn’t. The chips were hot and fresh at least, but both drinks were bad in their own ways. The L&P was watery, and the banana shake tasted like depleted uranium. Business Andy actually used to work at a Burger King a long time ago, and this was every bit as bad as he remembers.

excerpt:
Sweet chilli chicken calzone
Vegetarian stuffed potato
Banana smoothie

Coffee on the Terrace advertises that they are open until 2:30pm on a Saturday. So you can colour us surprised when we arrived at 1:10 to find the kitchen closed, and a member of staff bringing in the sign from the footpath. Luckily, cabinet food was still available. Unluckily, we ordered the calzone. Jesus it was bad, bready, dry, and flavourless. It wasn’t even really a calzone, do they even know what a calzone is? The potato was far better, but it’s hard not to be. The vegetables other than potato were nondescript. If you were wearing a blindfold while eating this and were asked what vegetables were in there, your answer would have been just potato. At least it was hot all the way through. The banana smoothie obviously had some banana syrup in it as well as a real banana. Not awful but not good either.

title: Long Black Cafe
excerpt:
Banana smoothie
Cheese and pineapple toasted sandwich
Beef burger with chips

A good toastie is a thing of true beauty, however too many cafes have the toasted sandwich as a throwaway, easy addition to the menu for no other reason other than because they have the ingredients. Long Black Cafe falls into this category. They had at least done a grainy bread instead of a plain white sandwich loaf, but there was very little love put into this toastie. We’re not saying this to single out Long Black Cafe, most toasties are like this, this frustration has been building for a while, and it’s time to cry shame on anyone who does this to the toastie sandwich. Crushed pineapple should not be used in a toasted sandwich, it’s too wet and it gives you a soggy inner bread surface. This toastie did have a good amount of cheese, and at least they cut it into triangles and not the dreaded and baleful rectangular slice. Our recommendation to cafes everywhere is to just not offer a toasted sandwich if you are going to treat it with this much contemptuous disrespect. The smoothie had quite a bit going for it, excellent texture and temperature, with a wide metal straw, it could have been a bit sweeter though. The burger was a let down for $20 in Woodville. These guys need to head down the road to Empire Sports Empire Sports & Garden Bar Restaurant to check out a burger that is 25% cheaper and 250% better. The bun was plain, the patty was of the dig-out-of-a-freezer-for-a-quick-Sunday-dinner variety, and the cheese was plastic. The salad in it was actually quite nice, and they had put it on the bottom bun, which is the proper way to construct a burger. Unfortunately, they decided to lubricate the patty on both sides with the melted sheet of plastic cheese on top and thick slices of slippery tomato on the bottom. As if to warn us of the trap that had been laid, the lid of the burger dismounted from the rest of it as the plate was put on our table.

title: Mission Estate Winery
excerpt:
House made loaf with olive oil, balsamic, and dukkha
Salt and pepper squid
Leek and cauliflower croquette
Wagyu beef brisket, miso custard, soba noodle and squid ink crisp
Creamed pumpkin tagliatelle
Duck breast with beetroot gratin and cumquat marmalade
Roast banana and caramel brûlée

Mission Estate is a beautiful historic venue, and as it was warm autumn evening we dined outside under the grapevines. We tried a lot of different dishes at The Mission, and they were almost all excellent. The weak links were the house made loaf, which was a bit dense and didn’t come with enough oil, and the tagliatelle which was just a tad bland. These were not bad dishes, it’s just that everything else was outstanding. Neither Business Andy nor the Fee-Rex is a big squid head, but we still knew good squid when we tried it. We are both big croquette heads however, and could appreciate that the leek and cauliflower croquette was top tier. It was delightfully creamy and crunchy, and had no stringy leek bits as can sometimes happen. The beef brisket was weird, but in the best way. The accompanying miso custard made us both reconsider our relationship with miso, which until now had been strained. The duck breast was so tender, so crispy, so flavourful, and so sweet, it might have been the best dish on the table the whole night. And the brûlée was a nice end to a special meal. We would be happy to return to The Mission any time.

Yatai is a little bit out of the way, but it’s worth stepping off the main drag to go here. The plates are shared, sort of like tapas style, and the restaurant recommends two plates per person which seems about right. Everything was just delicious. All the meals apart from the gyoza came with shredded cabbage on the side, which at first we thought was just a garnish, but truly elevated each dish. Our waitress did forget about us for a bit, but that didn’t bring us down, and the service on the whole was friendly. Bookings recommended.

title: Focal Point Cinema & Cafe
excerpt:
Beef nachos
Roast vege filo with salad
Liquorice allsort slice

Focal Point Cafe is tidy and good looking, probably due to being less than a year old. Unless it’s a hot day we recommend you do not sit near the door, which is the automatic sliding variety that opened and closed constantly letting in blasts of cold wind. Credit to Focal Point for serving something we’d never seen in a cafe cabinet before, the liquorice allsort slice. While this was very sweet, it was also yum and had a good sense of fun to it. The filo was good too, and while the salad initially seemed overdressed the dressing was very tasty so this was a welcome surprise. The nachos were unfortunate. The ratios were well off, with too much bland mince for the number of chips. The cheese was a solid layer on top making it impossible to dunk the nachos into the mince mixture. And it didn’t even come with any cutlery, so clearly they were expecting us to eat hot fistfuls of mince with our bare hands once all the nachos were gone.

title: Tasty Restaurant
excerpt:
Sweet and sour pork
Lemon chicken
Rice

Tasty Restaurant has a very authentic looking menu, but tonight we chose to go with a couple of honky classics which are generally a safe bet. We were wrong. The lemon chicken was ferociously sweet and yellow, and definitely void of any actual lemons. Rather than doing pieces of fried chicken, they’d gone for the vastly inferior giant slabs of chicken deep fried, then sliced, with sauce poured all over. The sweet and sour pork was a little better, at least they did little pieces of pork instead of half a pig sliced up. The pineapple was tasteless and the sauce has this unpleasant tang. Maybe we’d have been better off ordering the spicy duck blood with omasum instead of trying to play it safe.

title: Thai Chef's Restaurant
excerpt:
Massaman curry with braised beef
Lemon honey stir fry with crispy fried fish
Rice
Roti

Sigh. This meal was bad. The cocktails came first, and they were sickly. They were too sweet even for the Fee-Rex, and that’s saying something.  Next came the fish, no other dishes appeared. The fish was not delish. The fillets themselves appeared to be cheap crumbed hoki pieces from the nearby New World’s frozen section. Also from the frozen section was Home Brand mixed vegetable, carrot, corn, and peas topped up with a some unwelcome tomato and additional carrot. The only good bit was the pineapple where they had rightly used big chunks instead of little pieces. There was such a lengthy wait before anything else showed up that we had almost finished the fish, not that we wanted to. Then came the massaman curry, which didn’t taste like much other than sugar and almost comically dry beef. We were at least looking forward to the roti which we were hoping would be a reliable option. But somehow they even managed to ruin roti. It was unevenly cooked, tasted like it had been found under a couch, and they had even failed to cut it all the way through. If for some reason you want to visit Thai Chef’s Restaurant, bookings are highly recommended because they were inexplicably packed.

title: Noodles & Dumplings
excerpt:
Spring onion pancake
Fried thin noodles with BBQ pork
Fried fish with salt & pepper 
Fried vegetable dumplings

Friends of ours used Noodles & Dumplings to cater their wedding. We can see why. The food ranged from good to delicious, the people working there were warm and friendly, and we really appreciated their eclectic collection of mufti outfits. Best dressed male wore a dope denim jacket with a bumblebee on the back, best dressed female was in a crop top and high waisted super short shorts. The spring onion pancake was the weakest offering of the bunch, but it was by no means bad, and it was a three way tie for the top spot. The Fee-Rex doesn’t much like dumplings, but she was popping these ones like Tic Tacs, they were just delicious. The fish had an excellent batter, and the fish itself was real fillets, not the hoki composite BS you get at some other places, not naming any names as we’re not in the business of kicking Thai Chef’s Restaurant when they are down. The noodles were flavourful and there was a lot of them, a winning combo. We ordered way too much food for two people, but fortunately they had takeout boxes on hand as they were doing a roaring takeaway trade. FYI you order and pay at the counter before sitting down.

title: Wendy's Hamburgers
excerpt:
1/4 lb beef burger regular meal 
Chicken pretzel pub burger

This meal was a real mix of fresh highs and cheesy lows. The beef burger was very good, fresh ingredients, and a great ratio of bun:salad:sauce:meat. The fries were fresh, crispy, thicccccc, and neither over nor under salted. They had a pump your own sauce station, which was a great throwback to the 90’s, and the L&P was not watered down. The chicken burger was a tragedy. The culprit: a foul beer cheese sauce, which tasted like neither beer nor cheese. The burger was sopping with it, completely obscuring all other flavours. It is hard to believe that anybody would enjoy that sauce, and nobody would enjoy that quantity of it. The pretzel pub range is for a limited time only, thankfully.

title: Cheltenham Hotel
excerpt:
Nachos with beef mince
Fish, chips, & salad

The Cheltenham Hotel (the Chelty, as it is affectionately known by its loyal clientele) is a warm and inviting country pub, complete with a border collie sleeping on an old three piece suite, locals who get their own drinks, and a handle club that meets every Thursday. The food was okay to okay+. The nachos were a bit bland, however they were crisp all the way down, finally someone worked out that you shouldn’t be making them all soggy by dumping mince on top. In a surprise twist, the fish was panko crumbed but was unfortunately a bit fishy and processed. The chips were crisp with a tasty herbed salt, and the salad showed some effort had been made, including the addition of a cherry tomato and a slice of beetroot.

The waitress may have been blinded by this, as she didn’t seem to notice things like us waiting to order, or plates sitting on tables. We are being a little unfair here, as there was clearly too much work for a single waitress. Both curries were very sweet. title: Little India
excerpt:
Butter chicken with rice and paneer garlic kulcha
Paneer shimia mirch with rice and plain naan

The food at Little India is excellent. The butter chicken was delicate, and the paneer shimia mirch was unusual but very tasty. If we were only reviewing the food their rating might be higher, but we’re reviewing the entire dining experience. They didn’t get off to a good start when they forgot our reservation, although they did manage to put an extra seat at a spare table. Shortly after sitting down, we started coughing, and then other patrons joined in. Something akin to mustard gas had been released from the kitchen. We thought they were trying to teach us about trench warfare, but the waitress assured us that it was the result of cooking an “Indian hot” curry. This was clearly untrue as there was visible smoke coming from the kitchen at some points. They continued to wage chemical warfare against us and all the other poor G.I’s in the restaurant throughout the evening. They also forgot to bring out the one drink that was ordered at our table. Perhaps foreshadowing the wait for our meals, the drink showed up over twenty minutes later, and our food took over an hour to arrive. Complimentary poppadoms were provided, but these only arrived right before our meals, almost like an afterthought. We would have preferred gasmasks.

In other bad news, the Fee-Rex was given chips after ordering roast potato on the side, and the bÃ©arnaise was unusually foamy. These are rookie mistakes, and when you are at the top, you have to keep performing, there’s no room to rest on your laurels. Bookings essential.

The naans were fresh, which is not a given at the food court. However, given the way Shamiana were stacking the naans high and not rotating them, our naan freshness was more luck than good food management. They only had one bowl left when we got there, so the butter chicken came in a takeaway container which was slightly larger and there was enough of that sauce. So giving out enough sauce to properly saturate your rice isn’t an issue, they just choose not to do it.

title: Viva Cafe & Bar
excerpt:
Lamb moussaka with salad, rice, and Turkish bread
Chicken breast stuffed with mushroom, topped with bÃ©chamel sauce with salad, rice, and Turkish bread

We’ll start with the things that we could agree on. It was odd that both meals, although they appeared different in the menu, were almost identical. Two thirds of each plate was exactly the same. The rice was nice. And overall, the joint was a bit cold, with a nearby door letting in frequent icy blasts. We were divided on the rest.

Review 1: When it first came over, I had a strong whiff of French toast. I’ve never had that before when someone brought over my evening meal, and I really thought someone nearby was having breakfast for dinner. The sauce was the source of the odour. For some reason the bÃ©chamel was unnaturally sweet and nutmeg-ey. On top of ruining the chicken, I was displeased to find that the sauce had contaminated other elements of the meal. The salad itself was acceptable, classic, Turkish style salad, like what I’d expect to get with an iskender. While not offensive in and of itself, it was bizarre to combine with the stuffed chicken breast. I don’t have such a strong opinion about the moussaka. The lamb was fine, however the veggies were an indistinguishable mush.

Review 2: I thought the chicken was an unusual thing to pair with your classic Turkish salads. Particularly incongruous was the raw cucumber next to a hot stuffed chicken breast. However once the cucumber and tomato were out of the way, the salad turned out to be great. The chicken breast was pretty nice, and the sauce really didn’t deserve to get ripped a new one like it just did in the other review. The salad and co. paired very well with the moussaka which was absolutely delicious. It was savoury and hearty, and was just what the doctor ordered on a chilly night. Honestly I could have eaten that moussaka all over again as soon as I’d finished.

title: Columbus Cafe
excerpt:
Corn fritters with bacon and egg added
Vegetable stack

What is up with the popularity of Columbus Coffee? This chain of mediocre cafes has been around for more than 25 years, and they are everywhere. We have two in Palmerston North alone, and this particular cafe was doing a steady trade. This makes no sense, as the food here is on the bad side of middle-of-the-road, and the prices are exorbitant. We paid more than $50 for two meals and one ginger beer. That almost buys a house in Palmerston North! Worst of all, the menu is littered with predatory recommendations for add-ons. We foolishly decided to take these up, adding bacon and egg to the corn fritters. No price for the add-ons is obvious in the menu. We were shocked to find that they were charging $5 for two sad pieces of bacon, and $4.50 for a single egg. Why would anybody eat here when you could have better food for cheaper at Trio Cafe? The fritters were doughy, heavy on the fritter and light on the corn.

title: Gengy's Mongolian BBQ Buffet
excerpt:
Buffet-style meals

We were really looking forward to a walk down memory lane at Gengy’s. Last time either of us ate here we were both starving students trying to eat all we could and walk out with spring rolls in our pockets. The prices today reflect this proud history. It’s a bargain if you absolutely stuff your face, but for the more restrained diner, or really for anyone who doesn’t want to pop like Mr Creosote, the pricing is a bit on the steep side. We estimate $25 at most would be a fair price for what we ate, Gengy’s charges $33.99, not $34.00, but just one easy payment of $33.99. For this low, low price, you get to enjoy a buffet style meal with a twist. On top of a standard buffet featuring cold fish bites, cold onion rings, cold spring rolls, and cold chicken nuggets, you can fill a bowl with your choice of raw meat, vegetables, oil, and sauce to be cooked while you wait on a giant ring shaped hot plate. The meat was was as cheap and nasty as it comes, with all the gristle to match but they did have a good variety of fresh vegetables. They had plenty of sauces, oils, and topping bits, allowing many different flavour combinations. But wait, there’s more. All-you-can-eat, made-to-order pancakes, plus a dessert bar with cheap ice cream, five sauces, sprinkles, nuts, jelly, fruit, whipped cream, and butter. Top tip: Gengy suggests having peanuts or butter or maple flavoured sauce on a pancake, we discovered that all three together is absolutely delicious. Even though the food isn’t particularly good, that’s not why you eat here, it’s fun to eat at Gengy’s. Bookings recommended.

title: The Bees Knees Cafe
excerpt:
Macaroni cheese
Beef nachos
Banana smoothie

The Bees Knees has a real fussy old lady vibe. Not a surface is wasted, with old fashioned teacups cluttered amongst preserves, packaged homemade biscuits and greeting cards for sale. This is a small cafe with tiny tables crammed close together, it’s honestly a bit claustrophobic. The food was a disappointment. The macaroni cheese was incredibly bland, consisting only of a basic white sauce with macaroni in it and cheese on top. Perhaps their kitchen was too cluttered with granny junk for them to locate their salt, pepper, mustard, paprika, or anything else that might have made this meal not taste like pasty nothing. The nachos were no better, with watery mince and not enough cheese. The meals were small, which we were grateful of given the taste. They were at least affordably priced. In a surprising twist, the banana smoothie was the best we’ve had in some time.

title: Indian2nite
excerpt:
Malai kofta
Paneer makhani
Plain naan
Cheese & garlic naan

We’re just going to say it, one of these curries wasn’t a curry at all. The paneer makhani was clearly a can of tomato soup mixed with sugar and some leftover butter chicken sauce. It was very thin and the paneer was rubbery, dry, and highly cuboid; clearly store bought. It was at least cheap, but cheap food doesn’t have to suck. The malai kofta was a bit better, and they didn’t skimp on the koftas either. In addition to cooking some pretty questionable curries, Indian2nite also tried to hoodwink us in the naan department. Cheddar is a pretty flavourful variety of cheese, and if you replace it with something else, people are going to notice. Don’t bait us with cheddar cheese in the menu, then switch out the cheese in the naan with stringy and flavourless mozzarella. The nerve. The plain naan was as advertised at least, plain and serviceable.

title: Cafe 116
excerpt:
Beef nachos
Hash stack
Banana smoothie

Cafe 116 is better than their old-fashioned, designed-on-Windows-Publisher-‘95 signage would suggest. We drive past this place regularly and always figured it was a real dive. It is tucked away next to a dirt bike & jetski shop and just looks a bit sad from the outside. So you can colour us surprised to find that the inside was large and airy with high ceilings and a cosy fire burning. The menu was standard cafe fare, but done relatively well. The nachos had made some effort to double-layer their cheese (cheese on top plus a second layer of melted cheese half way down) which was appreciated. The mince was on the flavourless side but there was plenty of sour cream. The menu did state “smashed avocado” on top of the nachos, when actually there were just two small avocado slices. The hash brown stack was tasty, with the right ratios of hash to bacon to mushroom plus a perfectly cooked egg and some welcome pesto and balsamic. The banana smoothie caused some debate, with Business Andy making the accusation that it contained banana syrup (as well as real banana), while the Fee-Rex was not so sure. Flavouring issues aside, the smoothie had the correct texture and coldness.

excerpt:
Singapore steak
Vegetarian laksa

In many ways, Angkor is quite unremarkable. But it is remarkably popular, in fact, we’ve been turned away without a reservation more than once. The Singapore steak was very large, very sweet, and the large pieces of meat were mostly good quality with just a few chewy bits. The laksa was richly flavoured, and like the Singapore steak was a large meal. Speaking of large, the vegetables in the laksa were very large, and frankly it was a problem. Not only was no knife provided, but the cutting surface was a bowl of soup, even if a knife had been provided, it still would have been difficult. Don’t only partially cut up the vegetables into pieces that have to be bitten off a fork in several mouthfuls. Bookings essential.

title: Kabbaba
excerpt:
Lamb iskender with sweet chilli, hummus, and mayonnaise
Lamb doner with hot chilli, satay, and yoghurt

How dare you charge extra for satay sauce and garlic aioli? These are standard kebab sauces and should carry no extra charge over any of the other sauces. News flash, garlic aioli is basically just mayo. Maybe this was the source of the three customer complaints that we witnessed in the short time we were there, or maybe it was the absurdly long wait between ordering and eating. To be fair, the Plaza was positively heaving with people on the day we were there, so they were perhaps a lot busier than they expected. The food itself was acceptable. The doner was just the right size to actually fit in your mouth, and consequently was the right size for lunch. In contrast, the iskender was enormous, no Turkish bread came with it though. So aside from the busy food court setting, the angry customers, and the expensive sauces, Kabbaba just blends into the background hum of every other ordinary Turkish establishment.

title: Bing House
excerpt:
BBQ pork pancake
Beef & cheese bao bun

Eugh. This meal sucked, and they messed up our order to boot. The bao bun was the most offensive. The bun itself was doughy and sweet, the “cheese” was in fact a cheese sauce that didn’t resemble cheese in any way, and the beef was as chewy and dry as an old boot. The pancake was like a kebab, with a thin and delicate egg pancake on the outside instead of a wrap, however the pancake tore and spilled its contents everywhere. It didn’t help that it was wrapped haphazardly in baking paper, just tearing a bit of the paper off caused the thin pancake to practically disintegrate. There’s a Turkish joint not three doors down where they have solved this issue, the answer is foil. The filling was alright, with some crispy bits of pork crackling thrown in to add an interesting texture, however it was intensely salty. We barely finished this meal, looking down at the last bite of the bao bun was like looking into the black abyss of your own mortality.

title: Jimmy Cook's Kiwi Kitchen
excerpt:
Chicken burger and chips
Grilled vegetable and haloumi stack

Jimmy Cook’s has fallen into the classic hotel restaurant trap of thinking that if you put truffle oil in a couple of things and charge like a wounded bull, then you’re automatically a fancy joint. In reality, the decor was dated, the furniture cheap, the service clumsy, and the food decidedly meh. Our waiter was personable and friendly, our orders were taken promptly, and food came out fast. However, they also forgot to bring us a wine list, and when we asked our waiter what vegetables came in the stack he was clearly guessing, and only got one guess out of three right. Two if you count haloumi as a vegetable. Speaking of the vegetable stack, this was a horrendous rip off. The meal was tiny, which wasn’t a problem in and of itself, and we were warned that it was a small meal, but $25 for a sad and minuscule grilled veggie salad featuring some haloumi is outrageous. This was in no way a stack, the highest point was about 3cm off the plate, it looked like it had fallen over. It did taste okay at least. In contrast, the burger was huge, yet inexplicably was listed alongside the haloumi “stack” as a small meal. It was notably missing the beer battered onion rings that were mentioned in the menu, however we’re not really that upset that they didn’t show up as the table next door had what was clearly crumbed onion rings with their chicken burger. The type that comes with no guarantee of actual onion on the inside. They had also done a sneaky switcheroo on the advertised tomato sauce which was very obviously BBQ sauce. The burger itself was merely okay, the ingredients were cheap and not particularly well prepared.

A note on reservations. When we first tried to eat at Jimmy Cook’s we were turned away as they were fully booked. This would normally mean we advise booking, however trying to book dinner at Jimmy Cook’s involved so much waiting on the phone and so many transfers that we can hardly recommend it. Just show up and try your luck, and if they are full, then that’s probably for the best anyway.

title: Lina's
excerpt:
Lamb satay with rice cubes
Beef rendang curry with rice and salad

Prediction: Lina’s will close by the end of the year. This place is awful, and the lamb satay is one of the worst meals that we’ve reviewed. The ambiance was depressing. Everything was very obviously cheap, there were four different kinds of chairs in the restaurant, some of which inexplicably still had the plastic on them. The ambient music was a tinny radio in the kitchen, the plants were all plastic, and the place was echoingly deserted. Despite being open for a couple of months, the drinks fridge was completely empty, and drinks were not mentioned by our waitress at all. The beef rendang curry that showed up was very different to the beef rendang curry that we were expecting, it was pretty much just slow cooked beef in meat juice. That said, it was actually okay, the salad on the side was clearly a bit of an afterthought, but this meal was head and shoulders above the satay. The satay was listed as a “Chef’s Special” in the menu. We fail to see what is so special about skewers of extremely chewy lamb accompanied by a watery-with-chunks peanut sauce and giant bits of raw red onion. We suppose that you could call the rice cubes “special,” we’ve certainly never had anything like it before. It was cold (fridge cold, not room temperature cold) gelatinous roughly cut blocks of rice. And it was disgusting. We were pretty bummed out by the time we finished, but Lina still had one more surprise up her sleeve. As we were wiping our faces, desperate to ensure that we didn’t leave any satay residue for later, we noticed the serviettes were branded. With Anyavee, the last restaurant that died here. At this rate the next restaurant to occupy this cursed address will probably still have some of Anyavee’s serviettes leftover to use.

The hash brown breakfast involved hash browns, a massive deep fried sausage, streaky bacon, and two pieces of dollar loaf with a fried egg on each. A lot of food for $14.90, cost of ingredients: $4.10 by our estimation. The fish was so bad that we, card carrying members of the clean plates club, left more than half of it behind. The batter had split open in the cooking process exposing the fish directly to the oil with predictable results. Inedible.

Holy duck, what a burger. It was extremely juicy, flavourful, and unusual. We didn’t expect a middling hotel restaurant to push the boat out like this. The poutine was delicious, and it was so nice to have something that wasn’t just chips and tomato sauce on the side. The salad was boring and frankly there was nothing Mongolian about it. It’s a pity that the salad couldn’t keep up with the burger, La Patio’s rating was really dragged down by some dead Mongolian weight. When you visit La Patio, be sure to keep an ear out for their instrumental cover tracks, which ranged from Radiohead to Shawn Mendes, to The Beatles. Guessing what song was being covered was a fun challenge, not to brag, but we got them all except one.

title: Robert Harris Cafe
excerpt:
Keto toasted sandwich
Polenta, haloumi, and vegetable stack
Carrot cake
Banana smoothie
Mocha

This is not the Robert Harris that you remember from 90’s trips to get a pie and ham sandwich with grandma. While they were established in 1952, they have really moved with the times, and are now offering a good looking selection of both cabinet and cooked food. The stack was nearing perfection, had the tomatoes been cherry tomatoes instead of giant chunks of grilled tomato, it might have even been perfect. Roast kumara and pumpkin on the side was inspired and delicious, especially with their red pesto. It was a good high stack (check yourself, Jimmy Cooks) and it looked great on the plate. The keto sandwich was made from nice, fresh ingredients, no criticism there, but the cake was a bit of a letdown. The icing was overpoweringly sweet and the cake itself was a little flavourless. Classic cream cheese icing would have been a huge upgrade. The banana smoothie was also flavourless but did have the right texture and temperature. The mocha was clearly made with nice coffee, but was very sweet and - serious points deducted here - had no marshmallows on the side. The whole thing was a slick operation, the interior was clean and modern, the wait staff was very friendly and attentive, and despite being busy the service was fast. Nice one, Robert.

Another enjoyable experience at Yatai. We were surprised by the miso white fish, which doesn’t sound like much, but came with a delicious yuzu and miso sauce. It was the best dish of the night. title: Asia Restaurant
excerpt:
UPDATE: Both the Fee-Rex and Business Andy experienced some moderate digestive symptoms within 4 hours of dining at Asia Restaurant. We’re not certain that dinner was the cause, so we have not changed their rating, but it still bears mentioning.

Sweet and sour fish with chips and vegetables
Roast pork and vegetable curry on rice
Glass of milk

Asia Restaurant came from the 70’s, and they don’t make them like this anymore. There are several things that you need to know if you are going to eat at Asia Restaurant.

You will not be given water with your meal

You will be given two slices of dollar loaf buttered with table spread per person

There is no bathroom

Everybody eating there except you will be a regular. They will call the hostess by name, and will walk freely in and out of the kitchen

Cash only

When it’s time to pay, you’ll need to poke your head into the kitchen to collect the bill. Don’t be intimidated by the “Staff” sign on the door, that’s just a practical joke for first timers

The place is a little run down to say the least, and is honestly a little unwelcoming at first glance. But the food wasn’t bad and the service was friendly. The roast pork was pretty tough, the vegetables were boiled, and the curry sauce was okay. But the fish was well fried, and the sweet and sour sauce was reasonable. The dollar loaf was very welcome both for making chip sandwiches and to mop up the curry sauce.

Asia Restaurant doesn’t have an official website, but there is a fan page

So well done, Ronald, on becoming a global sensation and appealing to the masses. Not so well done on the food. The meat was a bit dry across the board, the fries were fresh but unsalted, and the hash brown was old and stuck to its paper sleeve. The “almighty” Texan BBQ burger looked a bit sad and had half fallen over in it’s box when it arrived via their new-to-us table service. This was probably thanks to the fried onion on the bottom, and although said onion did add a lot to the flavour of the burger, it took just as much away from its structural integrity. The cheeseburger was plain but inoffensive

title: Double Shotz
excerpt:
Rice and cauliflower vegetable pie
Red pepper, spinach, caramelised onion and feta tart
Carrot cake with yoghurt
Peanut and banana smoothie
Mocha

Double Shotz is a better establishment than the Z in its name would imply. Everything was tasty and affordable. There are many ways to make a great banana smoothie. A key factor is that it needs something, it can’t just be banana and milk. In this case, they’ve inventively gone with peanut butter. And it so worked. Had the smoothie been a couple of degrees colder it would have been perfect. The vegetable pie was controversial. Business Andy loved it, while the Fee-Rex was not a fan. We could both agree that it was an inventive and interesting addition to a cafe cabinet, which can frequently be a boring scene. The tart was sweet and delicious, with all components working well together. The cake was moist and tasty, but the icing unfortunately too sweet with not enough cream cheese. The mocha was great. It’s a common trap to just pour chocolate into a mocha, but that makes them way too sweet. Double Shotz knows this isn’t what you want, and held back on the chocolate resulting in a balanced drink, take notes Robert Harris. Still no marshmallows though.

title: White Horse Inn Motel, Bar & Restaurant
excerpt:
Pan fried fish, chips, and salad
Bangers and mash with peas and onion gravy

For the most part, the White Horse Inn stays within its comfort zone. There is a TAB, a handle club, at least four TV’s around the bar all playing different channels, and plenty of leaners with Tui towels on them. Their menu is mostly standard pub fare, but they unexpectedly also offer pan fried fish, which we were foolish enough to try. Pan fried fish only works if it is fresh, and this was anything but. We suspect it had come from the freezer. Rubbery, dry, really fishy, it had a nasty skin still on it, and even though it had probably been heated in a pan, it wasn’t crispy at all. The chips and salad were fine, but they are irrelevant when the only way that you can stomach the fish is to make each mouthful half tartare sauce. The bangers and mash was a bit better. The bangers themselves were the world’s cheapest pork or maybe beef flavoured sausages (who can tell?) from the discount bin, but they were really well cooked. There wasn’t enough gravy, although to be honest it wasn’t anything to write home about anyway.

title: Muffin Break
excerpt:
Feta, pine nut and spinach quiche
Cheese and onion toastie
Apple and caramel muffin
Banana smoothie

How did you do it, Muffin Break? How did you make the worst banana smoothie we have ever had? Artificial banana syrup, obviously, that’s a given. But there was somehow more. Most smoothies made from banana syrup end up tasting like a milkshake. Perhaps Muffin Break make their own signature syrup, from the peels of old bananas and the tears of a Cambodian orphan, creating a blend which is somehow simultaneously too sweet and too bitter. Undrinkable, which was a shame because we both needed some liquid to wash down the other disgusting components of the meal. The cheese and onion toastie never arrived. Instead, a cheese, ham and tomato toastie, which we definitely hadn’t ordered, somehow arrived. It was overcheesed, the ham was gross, and had gone soggy on the bottom from sitting too long on the plate. Perhaps this was because it had visited almost every other table before us. Despite the tables being numbered, the wait staff seemed to have no idea which meal went where. We were offered coffees, and then later a cheesy muffin, none of which was ours. The quiche just tasted like old spinach. The feta and pine nuts were visible, but not tasteable. We saw the waitress trying to give our quiche to another table; we wish she had succeeded. The muffin at least was okay. Perhaps Muffin Break had put all of their effort into making their flagship dish passable, leaving no energy for anything else. Pretty tragic. Although not as tragic as how many people were choosing to eat there. The place was packed! We need to band together, stop eating at Muffin Break, and let it die.

title: Indian Flavours
excerpt:
Malai kofta with rice
Dhaniya adraki paneer with rice
Garlic naan
Butter naan

Aside from the excellent mock kitchen for children set up in the play area, Indian Flavours doesn’t do anything to raise its head above the crowd. They did manage to do a few things that dragged them down though. We ordered a plain naan, so were surprised when the world’s oiliest butter naan arrived. No exaggeration, there was a literal puddle of butter under the basket when it was taken away. The butter naan had somehow also delaminated into two layers which was bizarre. At least the garlic naan held together, but it too was extremely oily. The curries were inoffensive but bland. The dhaniya adraki paneer had a nice ginger flavour, but not much else going on. The malai kofta was even more plain, apart from the two landmine-like sultanas that provided surprise flavour explosions. The kofta balls were the lowlight; doughy and flavourless. We did at least enjoy the greatest hits of Kishore Kumar wailing in the background. Perhaps the rest of Palmerston North aren’t the Kishore fans that we are, as we were the only diners there on a Friday night.

title: The Black Dog Kitchen & Bar
excerpt:
Black dog burger with chips
Grilled fish with lemon pepper, cherry tomatoes, chips and salad

The Black Dog is making an effort, and it shows. Many places like this that have a number of drawcards - open breakfast til late, have a full bar, a gaming lounge and serve reasonably priced food, seem to think “a certain number of people are going to eat here no matter what, so let’s just do the minimum we need to get by.” Not The Black Dog. Delicious homemade beef pattie and incredible structural integrity in the burger. Genuinely fresh fish, which they’ve bothered to cook a way that isn’t battered plus pair with a very flavourful lemon seasoning. These touches show The Black Dog is really trying to make nice food, and succeeding. It wasn’t aces across the board - unusually the chips were a weak link, being a little overdone and perhaps it might be time to change the oil in the fryer. The grilled cherry tomatoes seemed more heated than grilled. And they were stingy with the sauce for the fish. But these were relatively minor complaints about an otherwise very enjoyable meal.

title: Salt Bar & Restaurant
excerpt:
Karaage chicken burger with chips
Roast vege salad with slow cooked lamb shoulder

It’s not every day that you order an award winning burger, but that’s exactly what you get here. This burger won the Dunedin Burger Society People’s Choice award last year, and frankly we need to have a word. Either they didn’t serve the same burger last time the judges rolled around, or there’s something rotten at the Dunedin Burger Society. It’s a nice idea for a burger, with edamame beans, sesame sauce, and slaw, and the bun and structure were both excellent. But the chicken was drier than the Sahara, which ruined the whole thing. Speaking as people, it wouldn’t have been our choice. Onto the roast vege salad, and we feel the need to issue a warning. If you order a roast vege salad in the winter in the South Island, you will get snipped. Par-snipped. Bloody parsnip for Africa in that salad. The salad was already underwhelming - not enough dressing, an absurd amount of lamb, and lacking nuts or something that would give some texture, but to then have to wade through mountains of parsnip, it was just too much.

title: Catlins Inn
excerpt:
Beef nachos
BBQ beef & bacon cheeseburger with chips

Rolling into Owaka on a Monday night, we weren’t spoiled for dining choices. In fact, the Catlins Inn was the only place open, and was doing a roaring trade. Credit where credit was due, they had only one member of bar staff and she was running an extremely tight ship. Prompt, friendly, professional service, meals came out fast, and empty plates were cleared away quickly. Unfortunately, this can’t make up for the fact that the food just wasn’t very good. The nachos were passable – very cheap corn chips and bland mince, but not offensively bad. Unlike the burger, which committed a sin we are yet to report on businessandyandthefeerex.co.nz – the refrigerated bun. What self-respecting cook would pull a bun straight from the fridge and, without heating it, use it to sandwich hot burger ingredients? Between the frosty bun and the chilled salad, it was unsurprising that the two wafer-thin patties, which would have been average at the best of times, were dead cold. There’s no coming back from that.

Prompt, friendly, professional service, meals came out fast, and empty plates were cleared away quickly. Unfortunately, this can’t make up for the fact that the food just wasn’t very good. The nachos were passable – very cheap corn chips and bland mince, but not offensively bad. Unlike the burger, which committed a sin we are yet to report on businessandyandthefeerex.co.nz – the refrigerated bun. What self-respecting cook would pull a bun straight from the fridge and, without heating it, use it to sandwich hot burger ingredients? Between the frosty bun and the chilled salad, it was unsurprising that the two wafer-thin patties, which would have been average at the best of times, were dead cold. There’s no coming back from that.

title: Sal's Authentic New York Pizza
excerpt:
Nonna pizza (mozzerella, parmesan, garlic, basil) with chicken

We’re not experienced with New York style pizza, but Sal’s fare does meet the depiction we are familiar with from TV and movies; large (check), thin (check), floppy (check), had to fold it down the middle to eat it (check). The tomato sauce and general flavour was pretty nice, dough was a bit bready at the edges, but the real problem was that once again we were struck down by dry chicken. Given that we had paid extra as recommended in the menu to add chicken to this pizza, it was pretty disappointing when after one piece we’re thinking “wish I hadn’t forked out extra for a dry old bird to ruin this dish”.

title: Curry Guru The Malabar Kitchen
excerpt:
Paneer butter masala and rice
Butter chicken and rice
Plain naan
Cheese and garlic naan

Curry Guru was a mixed bag. On one hand, their paneer was truly excellent; soft, delicious, great texture, and the accompanying sauce was pretty good. However, the butter chicken had a serious case of tomato soup-itis, although it did contain plenty of nice chicken. Surprisingly the naans were the weakest link. The plain naan was too thick and doughy, and the cheese and garlic naan was very heavy on the cheese, very light on the garlic. The menu advertised the naan would be filled with cottage cheese, but it clearly contained copious amounts of flavourless mozzerella. It’s not the first time we’ve fallen for this bait-and-switch and we just don’t understand. Why mozzerella? Cheddar, colby, edam, any of the hard cheeses would have been better. Or, crazy thought, put in cottage cheese like you said you would. Shout out to their $10 lunch special, which was nearly the same size as the full curry and great value for money.

title: South Sea Hotel
excerpt:
Mexican bean nachos
Battered fish, chips and coleslaw

Despite being a Tuesday night during the off-season amidst a pandemic which precludes all international tourism, the South Sea Hotel was pumping. The food and drink was flowing, and everybody seemed to be having a good time. They undoubtedly benefit from being the only restaurant on Stewart Island that’s open during winter, and frankly food-wise they had kind of phoned it in. Starting with the positives, the fish was fresh and tasty in a well-cooked batter that wasn’t too oily. The chips were fine, but the coleslaw was a real snore, just cabbage and onion with no real flavour. And where’s the tartare! The vegetarian nachos were pretty miserable. Completely flavourless bulk pack corn chips, under-seasoned bean mix and too much cheese. Points for the guacamole though.

excerpt:
Pork belly and brie ciabatta
Cheese scone
Tan slice

We would eat cakes and slices at Courthouse Cafe all day long. The cabinet was huge and all looked delicious, the menu sounded pretty good too but it was not a large menu at all. The cheese scone tragically came with refrigerated butter, and not enough to boot but it was otherwise very nice. The pork belly ciabatta was, unsurprisingly as it came out of the cabinet, delicious, if perhaps a little bready. You may have had your grandmother’s tan slice in the past and think little of it, bless her she’s just trying to make you baked goods that won’t send you to an early grave. This tan slice was nothing like that - decadent AF with a huge midsection of caramel, nice biscuit base and crumbly topping. One thing to note about the Courthouse Cafe is that it is not open at the weekends, so if you are planning to visit, you’ll need to work around that.

title: The Gipsy Moth
excerpt:
Fish tacos
Buttermilk fried chicken with aioli

Expectations aren’t high when you’re eating at an airport, especially when the last airport cafe you ate at crushed all hope for the future. Imagine our shock when we were served some really nice fried chicken at the Gypsy Moth. Juicy, not too greasy, crispy on the outside, hot, and fresh. The fish tacos really didn’t keep up. They were too big, you had to Sophie’s Choice between a mouthful of too fishy fish or extremely bland tortilla and slaw. There was some guac and hot sauce in there, but they were such a non-event that they might as well have not been there at all. It was impossible to get everything in your mouth at the same time anyway.

excerpt:

Fresh burrata, beetroot, truffle and honey, walnut, and rye bread
Jerusalem artichoke, goat’s curd, coffee, hazelnut, and parmesan
Pork belly with celeriac and persimmon
Patate fritte with black garlic
Cos lettuce, garlic tahini dressing, and radish
Crème fraîche cheesecake, pear sorbet, vanilla poached pears

Perhaps the best thing about Kika is that you don’t even have to look at the menu. They have a “just feed me” option where they’ll pick you out three starters, a main with two sides, and a dessert. With matched wine or beer if you’d like. We opted for this and were extremely happy with everything that came our way. Don’t worry, you can specify “no seafood” or “no tomato” as needed. The fee-rex’s favourite dish was the duck waffle which was delightfully unusual. Business Andy preferred the artichokes. Bookings are highly recommended, we were very lucky to get a table without a booking, we were there ten minutes after they opened and while we were sitting there everyone else who didn’t have a booking was turned away.

title: South Sea Hotel
excerpt:
Fish burger and chips
Potato and celeriac soup with ciabatta

How can you serve us fish with no tartare sauce last night, then serve a fish burger replete with tartare sauce today? You clearly had some, so you can’t play the “it’s hard to get stuff delivered to Stewart Island” card. It was a nice tartare sauce too, and would have greatly improved last night’s meal. As it happens, the fish burger with tartare sauce was quite nice, it fell apart completely but that pretty much always happens with fish burgers. They assumed that we wanted the full portion of soup, we assumed the half portion would be standard for lunch. Future diners are recommended to request a half portion unless you are extremely hungry, because this soup was huge. The flavour was pretty good, maybe a little salty, and it could have done with a few more whizzes from the stick blender as there were frequent pieces of potato. Wouldn’t kill you to toast the ciabatta either. Still an improved showing on last night.

title: Dejeuner
excerpt:
Baked goat cheese, beetroot, rocket, walnuts and crostini
Venison with red onion, kale, butternut squash and juniper berry jus
Braised short ribs with potato gratin, mushroom cream, charred leek
Duck fat potatoes
Opera cake with maple and walnut ice cream

There are two important historical points you need to know about Dejeuner.

In 2020 the head chef at Dejeuner had a heart attack and they have a new head chef

In the late 2000s, there used to be a grotty basement bar called Uno at the site where Dejeuner now stands.

As is our custom, we arrived at Dejeuner without a reservation. We weren’t sure that we would be able to get a table, as we have eaten here under the previous head chef and knew it to be an upmarket, popular spot. The waitress walked us through a refined dining area complete with golden plate awards and quiet music in the background, down the stairs to the basement. What a difference. The first thing you notice is that you are alone. We saw a lot of reserved signs on the tables upstairs, and when we left, upstairs was totally full. Downstairs was dead empty. It was also cold. The wall paper was not wallpaper. Instead it was actual paper featuring an unconvincing brickwork pattern, barely stuck to the wall. There was neon lighting, green around the “brickwork” and multicoloured down the stairs. There was a framed photo of a wine glass decorated with diamantes. There was a $25 fake fire with who-are-you-kidding-flames flickering in it next to a bar heater. The floor was laminate boards that were warped and coming up at the ends which didn’t help our already wobbly table. The bar still had the word Uno on the front. There was a television playing a loop of heavily curated Instagram style video from someone’s 2017 travel footage. Snorkeling with turtles, waterfalls aplenty, the Eiffel Tower, all accompanied by upbeat beach resort pop music. The music and footage would have been right at home at a Club Med swim-up bar. The side of the basement that contained the bar was curiously empty apart from some stacked chairs. We learned why when were peeking in that area and inhaled, all these years later the smell of Uno’s toilets was still lurking in the corner. To top it all off, the wait staff regularly ran up and down the stairs with no apparent regard for how noisy this was. And we mean running - the male server took the steps two at a time.

In complete contrast to the decor, the goats cheese entree was splendid. Fabulous contrast of textures, a symphony of flavours, we’d love to have that again. The venison was also superb. It was perfectly cooked, tender, juicy, flavourful, and the vegetables paired beautifully. The duck fat potatoes were tasty, but were clearly wedges. The short rib at first appeared nice. But on closer inspection the gratin was undercooked and the beef was flavourless. The opera cake was very bad. The sponge was abysmally dry, it seemed like it had been sitting in the fridge uncovered for the last five to six days. The layers of coffee cream between the sponge were very firm and not tasty at all. We really had to dig our spoon in to break the cake apart, and the payoff wasn’t even worth it.

If you would rather not eat in the basement, then reservations are recommended, but you’d be missing out on a pretty special experience.
