title: Kapadokya Mediterranean & Turkish Cuisine
excerpt:
Open Adana burger
Beef and lamb meze platter

Neither Business Andy nor the Fee-Rex had ever tried dolma before, and frankly we won’t be trying it again. Be warned, that rolled up seaweed/leaf looking thing on the meze platter might as well be a stick of dynamite. Keep it away from your mouth. That said, the rest of the meze platter was really tasty. Shout out to the homemade falafel. Likewise, the open Adana burger was pretty nice too. We didn’t know what Adana was before tonight, turns out it’s spicy lamb mince made into a square sausage and cooked on a skewer, and unlike dolma, we’ll probably try it again. Whoever was mixing the chili into the mince needs a good talking to though, as the level of heat was quite erratic, from pleasant one mouthful to where’s-the-fire-extinguisher the next. As is commonplace with Turkish meals, both meals were generously sized and reasonably priced

title: Spring Patisserie & Cafe
excerpt:
Savoury scone
Chicken stack
Chocolate cheesecake

When we first walked into the Spring Patisserie, we thought it didn’t look much like a patisserie. There were far too many pies and sandwiches in the cabinet, and not enough tartes and choux pastry. Are those things in the pie warmer actually delicate cakes that just look like pies and sausage rolls? The food only raised more questions.

Why was the savoury scone so sweet? Why was the ham all in one chunk and not mixed throughout? That’s not how they make them in Paris. The chicken stack also lacked Parisian flair. For some reason they put a huge thick and solid layer of carrot up top, so when you try to put a fork into it or a knife through it, the innards just smooshed out everywhere. To make matters worse, the chicken was in giant unappetising chunks, and there was far too much mozzarella. In fact any quantity of mozzarella is far too much in a dish such as this, it’s a really bland cheese for a start, and when was the last time anyone wanted mozzarella on something that has to be eaten with a knife and fork? A real patisserie wouldn’t have made these mistakes. J’Accuse! Spring Patisserie is not a real patisserie at all. You, sir, are a plain Jane kiwi bakery, and not a very good one at that.

La cheesecake, tres catastrophique. Sorry, forgot you weren’t a patisserie. The cheesecake sucked.

title: Saigon Lunch Bar
excerpt:
Beef lemongrass bahn mi
Beef pho

You may remember our review of Saigon Restaurant & Bar where most meals came with chips, save that information for later.

Today, the Fee-Rex ordered a rice dish, and they were out of rice. Side note: how does anyone ever run out of rice? It stores forever, it’s cheap and readily available, it’s not like it takes a long time to cook (and frankly, they had time; there was nobody else there), it was 11:45am and more than one of their meals relied on rice. You’re going to have to cook some, so what do you mean, you’re out of rice? They offered us chips instead, and it was then that we joined the dots. Saigon Lunch Bar is an offshoot of Saigon Restaurant & Bar, and the apple doesn’t fall far from the tree.

As was the case in Saigon Restaurant & Bar, the food was so-so. The baguette was way too crisp, the filling was alright, but it was poorly arranged so you couldn’t get everything in one bite, much like the tacos at The Gipsy Moth. The pho was reasonable, while it didn’t stand out it was enjoyable enough. It would have been nice to have had some water with these meals, for some reason they just left it in the fridge behind the counter.

It would have also been nice to have a coffee, but we were informed that the landlord owns the three neighbouring eateries, one of which is Robert Harris. And apparently, only Mr Harris gets to sell coffee. Why they continue to advertise it on the menu is beyond us. It’s a chalk board menu, just rub it off man. And then cook some rice.

title: Indian Summer
excerpt:
Shahi paneer with rice and plain naan
Lamb rajasthani with rice and cheese naan

The Fee-Rex has long held a conspiracy theory that multiple dishes on a typical Indian menu are actually the same thing. Indian Summer deepened this conspiracy. Tonight we ordered a shahi paneer, described as “cottage cheese cooked in rich cashew nut gravy and crushed almond.” Sounds a bit like a korma, we thought. When it arrived at our table the waitress literally called it a korma. We knew it!! And it was a pale, bland korma at that. Similarly, Business Andy ordered a lamb rajasthani, descibed as “speciality of Rajsthan this unique beef or lamb dish cooked in chefâ€™s special sauce.” Chef’s special sauce my left nut. Unique my right nut. It was clearly a blend of Maggi tomato soup, some butter chicken, and sugar. We had the same exact dish at Indian2nite where it was called a makhani. The plain naan was pretty good, but the cheese naan was a nightmare. Half of it didn’t even have any cheese at all, the other half had way too much, and it was mozzarella to boot.

title: Sony Cafe
excerpt:
Steak, cheese, and mushroom pie
Eggs benedict with bacon

A lot of places like this aren’t very good, Sony Cafe doesn’t break the mould, they just do what all those similar cafes should be doing.

The pie had a nice flaky pastry, it was not soggy at all, and the chunks of steak were tender and not full of gristle although they were perhaps a bit large. The eggs were well poached, and they had drained them before putting the eggs on the nicely toasted muffins. The bacon was well cooked and there was plenty of it, and everything was covered in a generous splash of acceptable hollandaise sauce.

Those other cafes like this, where they have the cabinets and the little menu for cooked items are often pretty average. It’s pretty easy to just exist and make average food, people will come just because it’s an easy and cheap lunch. So it’s really nice to see Sony Cafe put in the effort to make good food, and given how busy it was in there, we clearly weren’t the only people who had noticed.
content:
Steak, cheese, and mushroom pie
Eggs benedict with bacon

A lot of places like this aren’t very good, Sony Cafe doesn’t break the mould, they just do what all those similar cafes should be doing.

The pie had a nice flaky pastry, it was not soggy at all, and the chunks of steak were tender and not full of gristle although they were perhaps a bit large. The eggs were well poached, and they had drained them before putting the eggs on the nicely toasted muffins. The bacon was well cooked and there was plenty of it, and everything was covered in a generous splash of acceptable hollandaise sauce.

Those other cafes like this, where they have the cabinets and the little menu for cooked items are often pretty average. It’s pretty easy to just exist and make average food, people will come just because it’s an easy and cheap lunch. So it’s really nice to see Sony Cafe put in the effort to make good food, and given how busy it was in there, we clearly weren’t the only people who had noticed.

title: Brew Union
excerpt:
Philly cheese steak burger with chips
Lamb rack with potato and pumpkin gratin, pea puree, and yoghurt harissa sauce
Ginger kiss cocktail
Salted caramel martini

The cocktails continue to impress, the ginger kiss was a little different this time around, we think they had added limoncello, and it wasn’t quite as good as we remembered. The lamb rack was perfectly cooked, and the gratin was delicious, it really stood out. It was unique, they had layered the potato and pumpkin together in the one gratin, yum yum. The Philly cheese steak burger wasn’t quite as good as the other burgers that we’ve had here, but was still very strong, and there wasn’t too much cheese in it.

title: Namaste Bharat Indian Restaurant
excerpt:
Sahi paneer with butter naan and rice
Malai kofta with cheese & garlic naan and rice

Namaste Bharat was cold, both in temperature and in the disposition of the wait staff. The Fee-Rex ordered a sahi paneer, wondering if it would be different to the shahi paneer she had last week at Indian Summer. The menu described the sahi paneer as ‘paneer with sauces and special spices’ which didn’t offer much of a clue. Turns out sahi paneer is the same as a shahi paneer, in that they are both essentially kormas. It may be that sahi was a typo in the menu. The only noteworthy thing about this otherwise boring curry was that it came with a bizarre sprinkle of grated cheese on top.

The malai kofta sauce was very nice. Unfortunately, the koftas themselves were basically two giant balls of mashed potato, and so were pretty stodgy and uninteresting, not like koftas we’ve had elsewhere. The cheese and garlic naan was pretty good, it did contain some mozzarella but it wasn’t the only cheese, and the garlic on top was toasted (a welcome surprise) and well proportioned. The butter naan was a bit thin but was otherwise okay.

title: Pita Pit
excerpt:
Feta & quinoa pita
Greek lamb pizza

We are Pita Pit novices. While the concept is simple (essentially Subway but with pitas instead of bread), we were ill-prepared and found ourselves panicked in the salad and sauce selection process. The pita wasn’t very enjoyable, and it’s difficult to know how much of that was our own fault. Were the salads and sauces we selected (fresh capsicum, carrot, beetroot, lettuce, grilled mushroom, cheddar cheese, hummus) a bad blend to accompany the feta & quinoa rosti, or was this pita always destined to be on the flavourless side, regardless of what we did? The Greek lamb pizza, which did not rely on our blundering choices, was great. The flavours worked well together, the lamb was tender, the roast capsicum yummy, and the thin pita base enjoyable. The stringy mozzarella caused some topping loss, which was a shame, but was the only blemish on an otherwise great pizza.

Pita Pit offers both dine-in and takeaway, but they’re not straining themselves to make dine-in an enjoyable experience. We were given one serviette to share between us, and no plate to catch the inevitable detritus from the meal. Perhaps Pita Pit think that they are creating less work for themselves by providing the bare minimum. This is clearly a false economy, as it causes messy food bits to be dropped all over the table, and with serviettes at a premium we naturally prioritised our own hands and faces over cleaning the table.

title: Lone Star
excerpt:
Burrrrrito (beef mince burrito with chilli rice and coleslaw)
Kiwi joker (ribeye steak with onions, chips, eggs, mushrooms, and coleslaw)
Jack Daniel’s chocolate fudge pudding
Snake bite venom teapot (vodka, Galliano, triple sec, Midori, orange juice, and cranberry juice)

Maybe our tastes have changed, but Lone Star isn’t like how we remembered it from 2004. Which, incidentally, is about the last time that teapots were cool. That didn’t stop us, in a fit of nostalgia, from ordering and then instantly regretting the snake bite venom teapot. Although it was reportedly the waitress’s favourite, it was foul. Way too much Galliano, not enough of anything else, and the pulpy orange juice looked chunky and gross in the shot glasses.

We stacked the deck a bit here by ordering two items that had been recommended by a friend, and while they were the two strongest dishes, that isn’t saying much. The steak was pretty reasonable, well cooked and not gristly, but they put the wrong sauce on it, and the coleslaw was just a slog to get through. The burrito was tragic, it had clearly been premade and then reheated based off the lukewarm temperature, soaked-in tomato sauce, and withered tortilla. The rice was incredibly dry and had not a skerrick of flavour to it, and neither did the endless coleslaw. The other recommendation was a very average chocolate pudding, with rock hard ice cream and not enough sauce.

Bookings recommended.

title: Cafe Jacko
excerpt:
Fish, chips & coleslaw
Brioche French toast with bacon, banana, blueberries, maple syrup and ice cream
Banana smoothie

At Cafe Jacko we experienced a BAATFR first - finding plastic in our food. This was an unfortunate blip in what was overwise a very nice meal. The fish was delicately battered, the chips well cooked, and the coleslaw tasty (apart from the plastic). The French toast was intense. This isn’t your everyday cafe French toast - the brioche was thick, soft and rasisiny, they had battered, fried and sugared the bananas, blueberries were a lovely compote, and who doesn’t want ice cream with their breakfast food? Delicious as this was, it was a lot and did become a bit nauseating after a while. The banana smoothie was a standout, and hit the big three of texture, flavour and temperature. Despite the plastic we would happily go back to Cafe Jacko again, and the lovely man at the counter (was it Jacko himself?) was extremely apologetic and comped the affected meal.

title: Thai House Express
excerpt:
Tofu pad thai
Beef massaman curry with rice
Roti with satay sauce

Thai House Express, emphasis on the express. This is among the fastest food that we’ve been served, right up there with Wendy’s. The roti was nice, but what has happened to the satay sauce? It wasn’t peanutty at all, more like a watery curry sauce. Speaking of watery curry sauce, the massaman curry wasn’t very nice at all. This dish is supposed to be rich and hearty, but it wasn’t rich or hearty, and tasted far too strongly of fish sauce and sugar. In contrast, the pad thai was yummy, and we were pleased to see that we were served a tofu pad thai, not a vegetable pad thai featuring tofu.

title: The Victoria Tavern, Petone
excerpt:
Sourdough with truffle butter
Battered calamari
Beef skewers with satay sauce
Roast half chicken with duck fat potatoes, broccolini and crispy capers
Pan fried gurnard with saffron risotto and crispy capers

Friday night and The Vic was pumping. It’s another up-market pub, but had a killer cocktail selection (shout out to the Ginger Kiss) and an interesting menu. The meals were a mixed, but mostly positive, bag. Top of the pile was the sourdough with truffle butter. The butter was salty and delicious and there was tonnes of it. They had also presented it thickly smeared across half the plate, allowing the option to dip or spread. Genius. The loaf was thickly sliced and piping hot. Worst of the batch was the beef skewers. Some pieces were rare, some well done, and the satay sauce was disappointingly bland. The calamari had a tasty batter and sauce, and wasn’t chewy, but wasn’t silky smooth perfect either.

The chicken was large. They were serious about it being half a chicken. Unfortunately this meant the meal ended up having a disproportionate amount of meat relative to potato and broccolini. The potatoes weren’t as good as they should have been considering they were duck fat, we expect crispy perfection and these just weren’t there. The chicken was pretty good, the breast was a little dry but the parts on the bone were spot on. The gurnard was a very nice piece of fish, and the crispy capers on both mains were pops of perfection. The risotto was forgettable and while not fully claggy it was on its way to clag-ville.

title: The Daily Grind
excerpt:
Beef burger with chips
Bruschetta
Caramel and chocolate slice
Banana smoothie

Let’s start with the positives. The bruschetta was good, maybe a bit much pesto but it fresh, well put together, and we would happily eat this again. The same cannot be said for anything else that we ordered. The banana smoothie came out promptly and was a good temperature, however it was too milky, it didn’t taste much like banana, or really anything else except milk.

There was a lengthy wait for the cooked food. Given that we were the only people in the joint, a 25 minute wait just doesn’t make any sense. At one point we thought we could smell something burning, so there might have been a do-over. When the food did finally arrive, we could immediately tell that there was something wrong with the burger. The patty was almost cylindrical, the buns were squashed flat and charred, and the whole thing looked like it was ready to fall over. Why do people do this? You want the meat to cover the whole bun, you don’t want a small sad dehydrated ball in the middle. The patty’s thickness also meant it probably took at least 20 minutes to cook, which will also be why it came out so dry. It was a shame that the patty and buns were so bad as the burger had some nice components like the beetroot relish and caramelised onion.

We had saved the slice till last, it looked really good. What a disappointment. The base was about twice as thick as it should have been, and was overpoweringly bitter and dry. The caramel was good, but in these ratios it just couldn’t touch the sides.

title: Hydro Eatery
excerpt:
Battered fish bite Turkish pocket with chips
Beef burger with chips

Real talk, Hydro Eatery, a pocket holds things. A Turkish bun cut in half, toasted and sandwiched with hot contents is a burger. Additionally, a fish bite can be eaten by a human in one or two bites. Your bites were so big that they were basically a whole fish. Furthermore, the stake that you put through a burger is intended to hold everything together. If that stake touches neither of the two giant pieces of fish so that when you pick up your pocket/burger the fish falls out either side, then that stake is pretty blood redundant isn’t it?!

Now that’s done we can talk about the beef burger. It was merely okay, a bit dry, and was not quite hot enough to melt the cheese. But at least the whole thing didn’t fall to pieces when it was picked up.

excerpt:
Onion bhaji
Corn fritter stack
Turkish orange cake

This place had a beautiful cabinet, we could have eaten out of it four times over. We appreciated that the bhaji was a little different, it’s not a common thing to find in a cafe cabinet. The corn fritters were excellent, cranberry relish on the top really elevated them. We found out that the unusual texture of the Turkish orange cake was to be expected, as it was made with almond flour. So while the texture wasn’t our favourite thing about it, given that it was proudly advertised as gluten free we really should have seen that coming. That said, the flavour was great, we would have preferred yoghurt on the side and indeed we asked for it, however the cream that showed up with it was a great accompaniment.

title: Oreti Restaurant
excerpt:
Duck thigh, with roast carrot purée, roast potatoes, broccolini, and a port wine reduction
Pan fried snapper on roast potatoes with broccolini and salsa

Twenty or thirty years ago, this place would have been very elegant, but it’s just starting to get a little tired. Speaking of things that are tired, we were exhausted after trying to order cocktails. Don’t offer a cocktail menu if three quarters of it is unavailable, and don’t reveal what’s unavailable in steps like you’re trying to hide something; we order cocktails, you tell us they are unavailable, we go away and regroup, order two different cocktails, you tell us that they are unavailable too. This literally happened three times until we were so broken that we just ordered an orange juice and a ginger beer.

The fish was pretty good, there was only one tiny bone left in the fillet, the potatoes were great, and the accompanying salsa and broccolini were fresh and tasty. The duck was really good, the port wine reduction that it came in was just fantastic. This was a good meal overall.

title: Pauly's Diner
excerpt:
Chicken burger
Honey butter fried chicken basket
Blue cheese & hot sauce fried chicken basket
Potato fries
Banana shake

Note that this meal was shared between four people.

Wowzers. What a meal. It was so good that we’re still buzzing about it days later. Everything was perfect. The shake was out of this world, how did they do it? Both the flavour and the texture were excellent, and we could both smash one right now. The fried chicken in the chicken burger was crispy and delicous, they didn’t try to stack too much other stuff in the burger, so even after passing it between The Fee-Rex and Business Andy multiple times the brioche bun held together.

The two fried chicken baskets were essentially the same perfectly cooked, succulent, crispy fried chicken with two different sauces. We can’t agree on which was better, but they were both fantastic. Even the fries stood out, everything that came out of that tiny kitchen was crispy, not greasy, and had been made with love. You can really tell when someone cares about what they are producing, and Pauly cares a lot.

There’s only four tables at Pauly’s Diner, so be prepared to take away if need be.

title: Tejano Cantina
excerpt:
Jalapeno poppers
Queso
Tacos: tempura battered fish, carne asada, and popcorn cauliflower
Loaded nachos with pulled pork

We made a terrible error here ordering food that was labelled with a red chilli pepper. That is on us, luckily it was only the popcorn cauliflower taco and aside from setting us on fire it was pretty good. The weakest taco was the carne asada which was pretty much all meat, and it was too much meat. Not a common gripe to have in a taco, but honestly it was excessive. The fish taco was good, and had a lovely sauce in it. The tacos were fantastic value for money, 3 large tacos for $20; we definitely ordered too much food. The poppers were great, exactly what you hope for, and likewise the queso was also pretty good, with great tortilla chips that had been made in house, and reasonable cheese dipping sauce. Like the carne asada tacos, the nachos came with a lot of meat, and were a bit overwhelming. Great chips, great guac, but the meat was too bountiful, and was unfortunately a bit flavourless.

title: Phil and Jo's Cafe
excerpt:
Steak and mushroom gourmet pie
Cheese and pineapple toasted sandwich
Banana cake

Options for good dining in the Plaza are limited. So far, the best we’ve found is Shamiana, and that’s not saying much. Phil and Jo’s was very popular, in fact many of the cabinet options were all gone by 1 o’clock when we arrived. Unfortunately, this didn’t prove to be an indicator that the food was good.

The pie was served in a large ramekin, with no pastry and a potato top. We assume this is what made it ‘gourmet’. While the flavour of the innards were good, and the mushrooms were distinct, it had been way overcooked causing the potato edges to be rock hard and the bottom of the filling to burn. The steak was really gristly and unpredictable. Phil, Jo, if you’re going to buy steak that bad just cut your losses and get mince instead.

The toastie was cooked alright, but the amount of crushed pineapple they used was barely detectable. Also, they obviously hadn’t wiped the sandwich press as we had a big blurt of relish from another dish cooked onto our sandwich which was unwelcome. The banana cake was pre-cut and plated in the cabinet, and was down to the last piece. It was bone dry on the outside, although the inside which hadn’t been exposed to air was okay. It had a thick layer of chocolate icing on the top which contained too much cocoa. Interestingly, it also had a layer of buttercream through the centre. As the outsides were so dry, any extra source of moisture was greatly appreciated. Had the cake not been so dry, this extra buttercream probably wouldn’t have brought much to the experience.
content:
Steak and mushroom gourmet pie
Cheese and pineapple toasted sandwich
Banana cake

Options for good dining in the Plaza are limited. So far, the best we’ve found is Shamiana, and that’s not saying much. Phil and Jo’s was very popular, in fact many of the cabinet options were all gone by 1 o’clock when we arrived. Unfortunately, this didn’t prove to be an indicator that the food was good.

The pie was served in a large ramekin, with no pastry and a potato top. We assume this is what made it ‘gourmet’. While the flavour of the innards were good, and the mushrooms were distinct, it had been way overcooked causing the potato edges to be rock hard and the bottom of the filling to burn. The steak was really gristly and unpredictable. Phil, Jo, if you’re going to buy steak that bad just cut your losses and get mince instead.

The toastie was cooked alright, but the amount of crushed pineapple they used was barely detectable. As the outsides were so dry, any extra source of moisture was greatly appreciated. Had the cake not been so dry, this extra buttercream probably wouldn’t have brought much to the experience.

Pan fried fish on ginger and kumara cake with Vietnamese slaw

Wow, what an incredible fish dish. Everything went together perfectly, it was sweet and tangy, the freshness and varied textures of the slaw were a great accompaniment to the softness of the kumara cake. This is the best fish we’ve reviewed yet.

The lamb rack didn’t quite reach the heights of the fish, but was still good. The lamb itself was very nice, and the oxtail cigar was fantastic, but the rest was quite forgettable.

The cheesecake was a disappointment. The cherry was undetectable, the texture thick, and the ratio of base to cheesecake mix off kilter. There was a nice vanilla creme with it, but it came with a very confusing strawberry sauce drizzled over the top of it.

title: Breakers
excerpt:
Chicken tender burger with chips 
Thai beef salad

We don’t want to say that Business Andy had a privileged upbringing. But this is his first time ever going to a Breakers. You do the maths.

Breakers is still a very safe place to bring children, tables of rowdy teens and people with unadventurous tastes. The place had kids running about, was very loud, and the menu was full of safe bets.

The burger had some issues. Construction wise it was almost falling over when it came out, requiring a rebuild before eating. The skewer wasn’t even through the meat! The crispy chicken coating was so crisp we thought it was either gravel or plastic on first bite. They’d gone overboard with the tomato - 4 slices! The ‘aioli’ in the burger turned out to just be cheap mayonnaise, and the bun was approaching stale.

The salad was better. The meat wasn’t gristly, and was only slightly overdone which frankly is better than average for beef strips in a salad. The dressing was tasty and they had lots of crispy noodles which was greatly appreciated. However, some of the lettuce leaves were too big, and there was a layer of ginormous thick cucumber slices, which had been cut diagonally rather than perpendicular They were like frisbees and one came out every time you put your fork in.

title: Boho Cafe
excerpt:
Creamy mushrooms on ciabatta
Tan square
Savoury muffin

The person who made the food at Boho Cafe loves food. And we love them. Everything was delicious, and Boho Cafe had taken extra steps to make eating there a pleasure.

The mushrooms were exceptional, the addition of caramelised onion really elevated the dish. They had thoughtfully put the mushrooms and sauce in their own bowl so that the toast didn’t get soggy, and unlike literally every other cafe on the planet, their butter wasn’t fresh out of the fridge and rock solid. The savoury muffin was a little unusual as it featured leek, but was soft, fluffy, and fresh, and had just the right amount of salty feta on top. The caramel to base ratio of the tan square was just right, and the caramel itself wasn’t overpoweringly sweet.

To nitpick, there wasn’t enough toast with the mushrooms, there was a hair in the creamy sauce, and they didn’t bring us cake forks for the tan square, so we had to use the mushroom forks. This is still an exceptionally good cafe though, and we are going again next week. Bookings recommended.

title: Boho Cafe
excerpt:
Fried chicken and waffles and maple syrup
Cheeseburger spring roll with coleslaw
Basque cheesecake

What a huge let down this was. We came in so excited, but it only one short week the magic had faded. This was still a good meal, it just wasn’t the great meal that we expected.

The fried chicken was pretty good, but the waffles that came with it seemed like they came out of single plastic sleeves at a supermarket. They looked really interesting as they were fingers of waffle instead regular flat waffles, but they were doughy, thick, and flavourless. There wasn’t enough maple syrup, and it was just missing something, like creme fraiche or, we don’t know, just something.

The spring roll was really tasty. It was super cool that it was just like a cheeseburger, complete with pickles, beef mince, cheese, and mustard. However some of the details were a little sloppy. The coleslaw was naked (nobody wants to eat plain raw cabbage) and the spring roll wasn’t quite hot, it was only warmed through.

The cheesecake divided us, Business Andy really liked it, but The Fee-Rex thought it was too plain and eggy. Some people might say that you should expect that from a baked cheesecake, but those people liked the Basque cheesecake. And where was the yoghurt or cream?

All together disappointing, perhaps because they were right up the top, there’s only one way to go from there. We still want to go back because this place has such promise. Better luck next time.

title: Beaver & Bear
excerpt:
Newfie poutine
Northern spice chicken wings with blue cheese dip
Fried cauliflower with ranch and spicy dips

Beaver & Bear used to be a fairly successful food truck, so most of what’s on the menu is deep fried and delicious.

We tried their specialties, and they did not disappoint. The poutine was so hearty, and had stuffing crumbs on top, apparently this is all the rage in Newfoundland. Frankly, it should be like this everywhere. The chicken wings were probably the highlight, they weren’t too greasy for a start, and they had a warm spice coating that went very well with the blue cheese dip. The fried cauliflower was very well cooked and came with a hot dipping sauce that was actually delicious, and that’s coming from people who don’t particularly like spicy sauces.

Bookings essential.

title: Rumour Has It
excerpt:
Fish, chips and salad
Chicken burger with chips
Banana smoothie

Rumour Has It that this cafe sucks. We can confirm that those rumours are 100% true. Not one element of our meals was enjoyable. The banana smoothie looked appetising when it came out, turns out that was an illusion caused by putting the drink in a pre-chilled glass. The smoothie itself was too warm and full of overpowering banana syrup. The fish was overly fishy fish bites, and the salad soaked in a foul dressing. The chicken burger was a structural nightmare, jenga’d up 5 stories high and impossible to eat as presented. Even after removing some of the chicken and re-skewering it still spilled out everywhere. The chicken was bone dry, the bun generically flavourless. It did contain a hash brown, which we feel is an under-utilised burger element, but that didn’t come close to saving it. Even the chips were offensive. They had about 10% the flavour of a normal chip and tasted like stale nothing. Yes they were unsalted, which didn’t help, but it was more than that. How exactly they achieved this feat we’ll never know, as we sure as hell won’t be going back to find out.

Kumara, chickpea, lentil and lamb stew with corn rice and yoghurt
Waffle with cream, vanilla ice cream and maple syrup

Sorry Little Savannah, but you’ve fallen from your pedestal. We let you squeak by last time and retain your 4, but some insults will not stand. The stew was such an insult. The meat was dry and the stew was bland. Also, it was served in a cast iron pot, with a separate plate for the rice and yoghurt. This meant the stew was thermonuclear and stayed that way, while juggling between the pot and the plate was awkward. A standard bowl or plate would have been better. The flatbread was excellent as previous, as was the espetada. The waffle was good but not great, just missing that little something to make it special.

excerpt:
Braised lamb neck crepe
Pork dumplings
Banana, peanut butter, and cacao smoothie

Despite a rocky start, our meal at Amayjen was fantastic. On arrival we were tersely instructed to present our vaccine passes “before we touched anything” like we were children with chocolate on our hands. They also took ages to take our order, then lied to us about the reason. The first server told us they were looking for their mask, and the second server told us that they were a member of staff down. Neither of these is particularly believable, as we had just watched them both have a long conversation together after taking someone else’s order.

Fortunately for everyone, the food was absolutely fantastic. The lamb crepe was meaty, hearty, and full of flavour. And the pork dumplings were excellent as well. The smoothie scored full marks for both texture and temperature, a rarity.

title: Fire Home
excerpt:
Beef and lamb iskender
Falafel doner

It was an extremely quiet night at Fire Home, maybe they had taken the opportunity to leave a skeleton crew. The one member of staff appeared quite inexperienced, she didn’t know where the buttons were on the till and couldn’t keep up with a normal pace of ordering. She also seemed not to know what comes with an iskender. The menu advertised meat, rice, salad, hummus, jacik, and sauce, however the plate contained only meat, rice, and sauce, and looked a little underwhelming. The meat was very dry, and we noted that their rotisserie meat stands were empty, so we assume this has come from the fridge.

Five to ten minutes later, when Business Andy’s kebeb showed up, we found out that this poor staff member also didn’t know how to wrap a doner. They really shouldn’t have been left there alone. The foil was all scrunched up on one side, it was completely wrapped instead of open at one end, wasn’t in a bag, and wasn’t on a plate. The net result was that you had to tear open a foil package that didn’t tear open well and was also too hot to handle. Opening the foil was like tearing a hangnail off your finger, you pull a little and nothing happens, so you pull more and then a whole chunk of scrunched side foil comes off bringing with it a long and painful tail that just ruins your day. There was sauce all over Business Andy’s hands, and a hell of a mess left on a food court tray. To their credit, the flavour was alright. And at least it had salad.

excerpt:

Memphis BBQ Big Angus burger
Original Big Angus (single patty)

Carl’s Jr is what Burger King was meant to be. The burgers were reasonable, the onion rings were actually real onion in a batter (shame about having too much salt). The Memphis BBQ was better than the Original Big Angus, with the crispy onion bits being a highlight. However, the patties were on the dry side, the sauce distribution and flavour in the Original Big Angus were poor. However, good construction and good buns were also at play. We appreciated the paper wrapped around the burger, but where the heck were the serviettes! Overall this was the best traditional fast food chain we’ve been to yet, although still not good enough to crack a 3.

title: Southern Cross Garden Bar Restaurant
excerpt:
Pork belly bites
Haloumi fries
Pan fried fish with asparagus, Anna potatoes, and lemon caper butter
Lamb shoulder with kumara mash, broccolini, and port wine jus

The service at Southern Cross is capital S Speedy. The entrees came out so fast that we assumed that there had been a mistake. The pork belly bites were tasty, but could have been better rendered, and the haloumi fries were delicious but came with an underwhelming sauce. They really did come out fast though.

The mains also came out absurdly quickly. The fish was meant to come with beans, and it was an unwelcome surprise when asparagus showed up. It’s not that there was anything in particular wrong with the asparagus, but the Fee-Rex is not a fan, and doesn’t think that restaurants can assume that it’s okay to swap one green thing with another without warning. Business Andy absolutely loved the little crispy fried capers that came on the side, and although they weren’t on the menu either, they were a much more welcome surprise. The fish itself was so-so, and the potato was pretty good.

The lamb dish was really good, the jus did a lot of work, and went with everything. It’s hard to go wrong with lamb, broccolini, and kumara mash, although it didn’t appear to have been roasted as was stated on the menu.

excerpt:
Beef sausage roll
Potato top pie
Churros

The decor at Coffee Plus + makes it look like a cross between a bar, a second hand furniture shop, and someone’s rumpus room. There is also a very sweet and very obese dog called Brie whom we liked very much. They didn’t make any of their food, they just heated it up for us. But that said, they had taken some care.

This was no casual microwave job, both the sausage roll and the pie were crisp indicating that they had been in some kind of oven. The churros were completely covered in cinnamon sugar, chocolate sauce, and caramel sauce, and while they were good, I mean come on, they were always going to be good, we’ve had better. The churros were the only thing that didn’t reheat well, unlike the pie and sausage roll, they really needed to be deep fried fresh.

If a place is named  Licorice Cafe, you’d expect a pretty great liquorice slice. As it turns out, the liquorice slice is not the main event here, liquorice is displayed on every wall for sale.

The slice itself was mostly just sugar, with coconut on the side, we couldn’t taste the liquorice at all. The contents were just mashed kumara, corn that you couldn’t taste, onion that you also couldn’t taste, and a small amount of some kind of herb that you also couldn’t taste. You know what, that’s a little unfair, there were a few sundried tomatoes on top, not enough, and there was a generous serving of sour cream on the side, it was nice that they weren’t stingy on that front.

title: Riverside Bar & Restaurant
excerpt:
Scotch fillet with chips, carrots and asparagus
Crumbed terakihi with new potatoes and salad

You don’t expect to find an elegant restaurant after driving past cabins, a trampoline, and a playground in a camp ground. It’s just so incongruous and unexpected, but that’s exactly what we found here. The restaurant is dressed up as a classy joint -  tablecloths, wine glasses on the tables and a dark colour palate. It was a nice setup, but just didn’t quite fit in with the swing sets and pool outside.

We liked the waiter, he was friendly and did a good job overall. He did forget to ask how Business Andy likes his steak, but they compensated by bringing out a steak that ranged across the piece of meat from rare to well done. Something for everyone! The meat itself was flavourful, but we wish they wouldn’t stack the steak on top of the chips, it makes them soggy with meat juice. The asparagus and carrot were top notch.

The fish was well crumbed but super fishy and the tartare was bringing no flavour. The salad was reasonable, while unfortunately some of the new potatoes were undercooked.

title: Turangi Bridge Motel, Bar & Restaurant
excerpt:
Venison pie with chips
Vegetable stack

What a venison pie. Excellent pastry, excellent gravy, excellent chips, and two excellent sauces. The meat was a bit dry, but that was the only misstep.

While a lot of effort had been put into the stack, it didn’t quite work. The heart of the stack was a feta and spinach patty that was good at first, but became a bit tiring. The stack had quite a lot going on, and all the ingredients were fresh. It featured a fried tortilla or perhpas it was a poppadum, either way it was fun but a bit greasy. It was hard to pinpoint exactly what went wrong, but about a third of the way through, this dish became a burden, two thirds of the way through, the Fee-Rex started to wonder if she’d finish it. In the end, Business Andy had to jump in to maintain our membership to the clean plates club. We can’t afford to have another LA Bakery & Coffee Lounge incident so soon afterwards.

title: Flat Hills Cafe & Tourist Park
excerpt:
Crumbed chicken burger
Curly fries
Mince & cheese pie

Flat Hills Cafe caters to the passing through crowd - cars travelling north from Palmy who are too hungry or lazy to wait for Taihape, families who need somewhere to stop for the kids to burn off some energy, and Intercity buses. Credit where credit is due, Flat Hills knows what it is and has provided. Heaps of parking for buses, motorhomes etc. A sizeable selection of cooked, cabinet, and readymade food (ice creams, chocolate bars etc). Accessible, plentiful and clean bathrooms. Fun stuff for children - animals to look at, a bouncy castle, swings, even a maze.

Unfortunately, the food just isn’t that good. The highlight was the curly fries - oh my God there were so many big curlies. We’ve all been disappointed before when you buy a bowl of ‘curly fries’ that is actually a bowl of sad half moons with maybe one 520 degree curly. Not this bowl, it was mostly real curlies, an absolute delight. But it was downhill from there. The accompanying aioli was flavourless and had a little skin on the top like it had been pre-poured. The pie had good pastry on top, but not so good for the base and a distinct I’ve-been-in-this-warmer-for-some-time flavour and texture. The burger was sad. Not only did it not contain any onion rings as advertised, it was poorly constructed, had unwelcome surprise tomato and just didn’t taste very good.

title: Cafe Cuba
excerpt:
Campfire smash
Cauliflower tacos
Banana smoothie
Passionfruit smoothie

Cafe Cuba has been one of the most popular cafes in Palmerston North for the past 20 years. They have a diverse menu, speedy service and a reputation for being reliably good. In the Fee-Rex’s expert opinion, it was home to the best smoothie in Palmerston North. We say was as unfortunately the smoothie game has slipped a bit. Don’t get us wrong, they’re still good, but they are no longer great. The passionfruit smoothie used to be tangy and creamy, really cool and thick with honey down the sides. Today’s passionfruit smoothie was almost too tangy, much less creamy with more of a juice consistency. The banana smoothie was perfectly acceptable, but lacked in va va voom.

The campfire smash, which is egg, potato, onion, spinach all cooked up together with a piece of ciabatta, was again good but not great. The tacos were disappointing, plain and thoughtless. They seemed like the kind of tacos you would make and home, eat then go “well, at least I’m not hungry anymore but I won’t make that again.”

Step up Cafe Cuba! You’ve earned a 3 rating today but we know you can do better.

Bookings recommended.

title: Chada Thai
excerpt:
Curry puffs
Tofu pad thai
Lamb massaman curry with rice
Caramel bubble tea

What a weird pad thai. Admittedly it was a vegan pad thai, so we were prepared for it to be a little different (no egg, maybe a little different flavour from no fish sauce). But veganism doesn’t preclude the pad thai staples of peanuts and lemon, both of which were absent. And you certainly don’t make up for a lack of animal products by drowning the dish in oil, which this was. Very disappointing.

The curry was better, with a nice sauce and meat that was tender, pretty reasonable on the lamb-you-find-in-a-cheap-curry scale. Peanuts were again a problem. There were upleasant peanut sinkers all at the bottom of the meal which had been “toasted” by someone who didn’t appreciate toasted peanuts. They had been grilled at way too high a temperature for a very short time, which had served just to put a bit of colour on the outside of what were in essence raw peanuts. For some reason the caramel bubble tea tasted like coffee as much as caramel. At least the curry puffs were good, nice pastry and flavour.

title: Cafe Brie
excerpt:
Lamb’s fry with bacon
Steak salad with feta balls
Banana smoothie

Cafe Brie was a real mix of the good, the bad, and the ugly.

The good: 
The smoothie was one of the best that we have reviewed. Understated, cold, perfectly smooth, and utterly delicious. 
The feta balls were fantastic and unexpected, a real treat.
The brown onion and mushroom jus that came with the lamb’s fry was dark, hearty, and very tasty.

The bad:
The steak was overcooked, we asked for medium but received well done steak.
The liver was unevenly cooked, most was a bit overdone, and a part of it was quite underdone.

The ugly:
The kumara. It was a bit overdone when it was roasted, and from the texture of it, that was at least three days ago. They were hard as rocks, and very unpleasant. And this was a real shame because the kumara is often the bit of a salad that you really look forward to.

title: Noodles & Dumplings
excerpt:
Sweet and sour pork
Lamb stir fry with bao buns
Brown sugar bubble tea

You’d think that we would learn our lesson after ordering way too much food last time we ate here. And to be fair, we ordered half as many dishes this time, but we were similarly left with another whole meal once we had finished eating. Next time we’re ordering one dish, and maybe a couple of dumplings on the side if we’re really hungry.

The sweet and sour pork had a bit of a crunchy batter on it, was covered in a tasty sauce, and came with carrot and onion. The carrot was sliced really thin and was thus delicious, apart from a few pieces that almost seemed like they were just a bit old. The onion could have used a few more minutes frying. The bao buns were excellent, fluffy, spongy, and fresh, and while the lamb stir fry was really nice and really fun to eat, this was a larger meal than was indicated in the menu picture (10 bao buns!). The bubble tea was quite nice, very sweet, but then it was sugar flavoured. It was also forgotten, and the waitress was super apologetic when we asked for it.

title: Provenance
excerpt:
Bruschetta
Beef tartar
Fries with truffle and parmesan
Seasonal greens - cabbage
Korean fried chicken
“Lemon pie” with sorbet

This place is really made for sharing, they offer small plates, which is all we ordered, and large plates which serve two to three people. Even the desserts are made to be shared, so it’s tapas really, even if they don’t say that they are. Speaking of sharing, if you are hoping to share a conversation, be aware that the acoustics in Provenance are pretty bad. The general noise level was so loud that we struggled to hear each other at times.

The food was excellent, it is on the fancy side but not overpriced, apart from the dessert which was a total rip-off. The bruschetta was a little different, it came with roast garlic and whole roast tomatoes for a “some assembly required” dish.

The beef tartar was very flavoursome, and was accompanied by a host of unusual but welcome bedmates. The fries really stood out, they had gone crazy with the parmesan and truffle oil, and the truffle butter on the side was just divine. Honestly it was a struggle not to mop up the remainder with our fingers. The chicken had a sweet chilli vibe, and didn’t have a thick crispy coating like a lot of fried chicken does. So it was a bit different to what

we expected, but was delicious nonetheless.

The lemon pie was their only misstep. It was completely deconstructed, and had way more sorbet than anything else. While the ingredients were all excellent, we would have preferred half the sorbet, and double the amount of the other components. Bookings recommended.

title: Cravings Cafe
excerpt:
Crispy chicken burger with curly fries
Kumara rosti with haloumi and egg
Banana smoothie

If you are pregnant, then this is the cafe for you, situated right in the birthing complex, and full of pregnant women. Maybe not full to the brim, but there was definitely an overrepresentation of gravid uteri the day that we were there.

The food at Cravings Cafe was actually pretty good, and there were plenty of other things available that we would have liked to try. The chicken was very crispy, perhaps a little dry, but the burger overall was excellent. Very well constructed, and the curly fries, which come standard with the burger were top notch. The menu didn’t even say that the fries were curly, but damn were they curly, with several very large curlies present. The rosti was made with orange kumara rather than the usual purple which was a nice change. The haloumi was well cooked but very thin, too thin to squeak, as it turned out.

The banana smoothie wasn’t good at all, unfortunately. It wasn’t a banana smoothie at all, it was some kind of mix of tropical fruits and was just very sweet. The great texture and temperature were hard to appreciate with that flavour.

title: Bay of Many Coves Resort
excerpt:
Grazing platter
Duck liver parfait
Tomato and mozzarella
Eye fillet with roast kumara and seasonal vegetables
Pan fried chicken with mashed potato and seasonal vegetables
Dark chocolate tart with pop rocks
Mille-feuille

Bay of Many Coves is a luxury resort in the Marlborough sounds. While we will confine our review to their meals, we will say that our high rating of their food reflects our opinion of the resort as a whole - absolutely fantastic. Note that we are reviewing their guest menus, available exclusively to guests of the resort. There is also a cafe on site where non-guests can visit to dine, but we didn’t eat there because we are too good to mix with that sort of riff-raff. There is no fixed menu at Bay of Many Coves, the meals change based on availability and the chef’s preference.

The charcuterie board we had for lunch was intense, best we’ve ever had. There was so much variety, generally four or five different types of everything eg there was a blue cheese, Camembert, some cheese with wax and some other hard cheese, then four different crackers, for meats there were two different salamis, plus ham and some kind of hot pork, there were apricots, figs, apple, grapes, dates, plus tomatoes, hummus, beetroot dip, macadamias, cashews. It was great fun trying all the different combinations and somehow everything seemed to work together pretty well. It was also beautifully presented on fern fronds.

The tomato and mozzarella was beautifully presented and flavourful. The parfait was tasty but way too much, could have used about half of that. The eye fillet was perfectly cooked and succulent. Some kind of marmite-esque blobs were on the plate and they were a flavour explosion. The mash with the chicken was a standout, don’t know what was in it but it was really good, perhaps the only thing that wasn’t pretty much perfect was the chicken which was slightly dry.

The mille-feuille was perfection, deconstructed and imaginative, every bite was heaven. The dark chocolate tart was one of the best desserts that The Fee-Rex has ever had, the tart filling was molten chocolate with golden pop rocks, and it was perfectly paired with fresh berries, crushed meringue and ice cream.

Bay of Many Coves is a luxury resort in the Marlborough sounds. While we will confine our review to their meals, we will say that our high rating of their food reflects our opinion of the resort as a whole - absolutely fantastic. Note that we are reviewing their guest menus, available exclusively to guests of the resort. There is also a cafe on site where non-guests can visit to dine, but we didn’t eat there because we are too good to mix with that sort of riff-raff. There is no fixed menu at Bay of Many Coves, the meals change based on availability and the chef’s preference.

The charcuterie board we had for lunch was intense, best we’ve ever had. There was so much variety, generally four or five different types of everything eg there was a blue cheese, Camembert, some cheese with wax and some other hard cheese, then four different crackers, for meats there were two different salamis, plus ham and some kind of hot pork, there were apricots, figs, apple, grapes, dates, plus tomatoes, hummus, beetroot dip, macadamias, cashews. It was great fun trying all the different combinations and somehow everything seemed to work together pretty well. It was also beautifully presented on fern fronds.

The tomato and mozzarella was beautifully presented and flavourful. The parfait was tasty but way too much, could have used about half of that. The eye fillet was perfectly cooked and succulent. Some kind of marmite-esque blobs were on the plate and they were a flavour explosion. The mash with the chicken was a standout, don’t know what was in it but it was really good, perhaps the only thing that wasn’t pretty much perfect was the chicken which was slightly dry.

The mille-feuille was perfection, deconstructed and imaginative, every bite was heaven. The dark chocolate tart was one of the best desserts that The Fee-Rex has ever had, the tart filling was molten chocolate with golden pop rocks, and it was perfectly paired with fresh berries, crushed meringue and ice cream.
address: Queen Charlotte Sound, Private Bag 382, Picton 7250

title: Chinatown Chinese Restaurant
excerpt:
Buffet

Chinatown Chinese Restaurant offers both a buffet and an a la carte menu. As we walked in the dude said “buffet?” We didn’t know better so we went with it, but when we looked out into the restaurant, we saw a bit of a trend appear. There was a few tables where people had ordered off the menu, and all but one was Asian diners. We suspect that they knew something that we didn’t.

The buffet wasn’t all bad, the stand outs were the vegetarian noodles, the fish bites, and the chicken wings. Standing out for the wrong reasons were the pan fried dumplings, the BBQ pork, and the pork curry. The rest of the things that we tried were middling to bad, the prime example of this category was the under seasoned onion rings.

There was dessert on offer, which was nice, the carrot cake was the best part, the cheesecake, the worst by a considerable margin.

title: London Quay Cafe
excerpt:
Fresh fruit salad with Greek yoghurt
Mocha

The problem with cafe breakfast is that it’s all the same, but nowhere is this more true than at London Quay Cafe. We’re sure that you could guess every single thing that was on the menu. Take a few wild guesses, we’ll wait.

Toasted muesli: check

Eggs Benedict: check

Bacon and eggs: check

Big breakfast: check

The lunch menu had a couple of things that were a little more interesting, but this breakfast menu was just despairingly unimaginative. To make matters worse, there was no Greek yoghurt, or yoghurt of any nationality with our fruit salad, and the mocha wasn’t very nice either. We will say that the salad was fresh, and was a good mix of different fruit; it wasn’t just all rock melon.

A note about music. We like Nelly feat. Kelly Rowland’s 2002 smash hit Dilemma as much as the next guy, nay, more than the next guy, but it was oppressively loud. Perhaps if they had turned the volume of the music down, and the volume of the menu up we would have had something nice to say.

title: Toastie Lords - Picton
excerpt:
Ivan toastie: pastrami, sauerkraut, pickles, cheese
Custard filled donut

After our misadventures earlier that morning at London Quay Cafe, you’ll not be surprised to hear that we were still in the market for breakfast. We spied a little toastie place two doors down and boy are we glad that we did.

The menu was small but innovative, there were salmon toasties, tuna toasties, and vegan kimchi toasties to name a few, and the toasties themselves were just excellent. Great size, perfectly cooked, and it’s the little details. There were four different kinds of cheese in each toastie, but there wasn’t too much cheese somehow. In fact the whole thing was very well balanced, the sauerkraut wasn’t overpowering, and even the pickles were in just the right quantity. Normally The Fee-Rex doesn’t like either of those ingredients, but today they were welcome.

To top it all off, the donut was fresh, soft, neither too sweet nor too big. And the vanilla custard filling was divine.

Much like Pauly’s Diner, seating is limited, and while the food is simple, it’s made with care and attention. Unlike Pauly’s Diner, there’s a large waterfront area with plenty of seating and spectacular views of the sounds just over the road. We wish there were more places like these two, it turns out that you don’t need to be a Michelin starred restaurant to serve excellent food, you can get a 4 rating from us with just fried chicken or toasted sandwiches.

title: Hungry Horse Cafe
excerpt:
Smashed avo on toast with a poached egg
Baked potato with mince

We’ll talk about these meals in the order that they arrived.

The smashed avo on toast was middling, the toast itself was thick, soft, and fresh. It came with a very welcome slice of lemon, which paired well with the avocado itself. Unfortunately, the poached egg was underdone and a bit sloppy. And extra unfortunately, there was a huge piece of lettuce under the avo, on the toast. We really don’t know who wants this, it was entirely unnecessary.

This space represents the gap between us finishing the avo on toast, and the arrival of the baked potato.

The potato itself was not underdone, but lacked fluffiness. We carefully avoided the vegetarian mince option because it contained red beans and chickpeas, so we were quite upset when the beef mince arrived with both red beans and chickpeas. Admittedly these both didn’t taste like much, but that’s not a compliment. Could have used a little more sour cream, extra points for the sweet chilli sauce on the top.

title: Cafe Royale
excerpt:
Big breakfast
Jackfruit burger

We haven’t been somewhere this shambolic since The Cooperage Cafe, and Cafe Royale was even worse. When we arrived we were fourth in the queue. Ten minutes later we were still fourth in the queue. It was immediately obvious that the cafe was disastrously understaffed, with just two servers running around with their heads on fire instead of taking the orders of the people who were waiting. As can happen when the world is ending, these two were just doing the next thing that appeared in front of them like putting chairs nicely around tables, and stacking the menus in their holder. Priorities, ladies!

There was a bizarre queuing system at play. You had to bags a table by leaving your coat or umbrella on it before then queuing up for all eternity. We suppose that they wanted to avoid people getting in the queue, waiting, and then finding out that there were no tables, but frankly they were causing that problem themselves with their glacial service.

We had been standing around in the queue for quite a long time when it finally started to move. We were given menus and only one minute later expected to order when we found ourselves at the fabled front of the queue facing a harassed looking server. Perhaps they cater exclusively to speed readers, because the menu was the most packed in and poorly laid out four pages that we’ve ever seen. Neither of us had read even half the menu, and we panic picked the first thing that sounded alright. We could see the flames around the server’s head begin to burn hotter and brighter as she struggled to find what Business Andy had ordered in the POS system. We had to point it out on the physical menu, at which time we found out that it wasn’t actually available, not just that day, but ever. Cross it out you numptys!

Business Andy was scanning for something new to order when he was accosted by the question, “are you vegan?” After answering no, the menu was literally snatched out of his hands by the server, who was completely engulfed in flames at this point, and cried shrilly “that’s the vegan menu!” While we appreciated that she was attempting to simplify what was a very stressful process, non-vegans are actually allowed to order vegan food. In fact we had just ordered two vegan meals right in front of her. The flames were licking at us, and we panic ordered a big breakfast without reading through what was in it.

The wait for the food wasn’t as long as you might have thought. The burger was plated up really nicely, with a blob of something like mayonnaise on top of it, and a smear of beetroot puree on the plate. If you thought there was something wrong with that sentence, there was. That stuff was meant to be in the burger. Do you expect us to dip the burger in the beetroot smear and then get blobbed in the nose by the mayo? Without the missing components, the jackfruit was flavourless, and the bun was extremely chewy.

The big breakfast was completely ruined by the presence of a bean and tomato chowder. Upon reflection, we believe this was meant to be the chef’s bourgeoise take on baked beans. Fail. Not only did this taste like a combination of tinned tomatoes and nothingness, but its juice had spread across the entire plate, infecting every other food item. This was a real shame as some of it looked pretty good, but that tomato juice was the kiss of death. At least we salvaged the bread before it could be defiled, and it quite nice, as were the cherry tomatoes which had been well roasted. We can see the chef was trying, but maybe he was trying too hard. Different is not always better.

title: Best Ugly Bagels
excerpt:
Yodi bagel: pastrami, Swiss cheese, mustard, pickle
Jellytip bagel: chocolate, raspberry jam, whatever that white stuff was

While they did their best to emulate the venerable jelly tip ice cream, Best Ugly Bagel fell a bit short here. The chocolate sauce wasn’t particularly nice, the jam was too sweet, and the chocolate bagel was a mistake, they should have just gone for a plain bagel here and let the toppings do the talking.

The yodi bagel was quite a bit nicer, our only real complaint is that it was a bit too oily. Business Andy, a true pickle maniac, would have preferred a bit more pickle, but he says that about everything.

title: Hayz at the Anchorage
excerpt:
Half roast mutton bird with stuffing, blueberry jus, seasonal vegetables, and mash
Ribs with salad and chips

Dining options are limited in Bluff. In fact, unless you want to eat a toastie and chips while being called a Covid Nazi at the local anti-vax hotspot, The Eagle, Hayz at the Anchorage is your only choice.

This restaurant embraces local delicacies. Along with the expected Bluff Oysters, there are also paua wontons, sweetbreads, whitebait, and mutton bird. Feeling adventurous, and keen on some local fare, the Fee-Rex decided to try mutton bird for the first time. It turns out that mutton bird, which is a sea bird in the shearwater family, is hella fishy. Even the smell is that of fish, and quite strong. It does look like mutton, which is perhaps where it gets the name, but it tastes like fish.

The flavour of the mutton bird has not been considered as part of the rating. We went out on a limb, and the restaurant can’t be penalised because we ordered something that just wasn’t us. That said, the rest of the meal was pretty bad. The stuffing was plain, and very dry. Other than a few (cold) blueberries on the plate, the jus was neither to be seen nor tasted. The mash was the best part, and the “seasonal” vegetables, the worst. We didn’t realise that boiled frozen vege mix had a season! For $40, in Bluff no less, we expect fresh vegetables.

The ribs were dry, although they did come with quite a nice sauce, and plenty of it, which did help some. The ribs were sitting in top of a big ol’ pile of chips, which ordinarily we are all for, but there were some problems with these chips. You know when you’re hung over on a Sunday morning, and your pour your McCain frozen chips into a roasting dish and slam them in the oven after finally falling out of bed just after 11am, and then you are ready for chips way before they are ready for you, so you get them out, half done, not crispy at all in fact a little soggy, those chips are full of sadness, and after eating them, so are you. That’s exactly what these chips were like, and frankly our disappointment is immeasurable. There was a little bit of salad on the side which was reasonable, but it was as much as afterthought as every salad that’s ever been on the side of a plate of ribs and chips has ever been.

title: Indian Sweets & Snacks
excerpt:
Chicken jalfrezi
Malai kofta
Plain naan
Jalebi
Gulab Jamun

Indian sweets and snacks offers a full curry and naan menu as well as some Thai and Chinese options. However we theorise that all these main meals are really an afterthought, with the sweets and snacks (of which there is a wide variety across two deli cases and are sold by the kilo) being the star. It would certainly explain the quality.

Firstly, the curries were too hot, especially the jalfrezi. We ordered mild, very clearly. In fact, he asked us twice. But what we received was definitely not mild and Business Andy had a bad case of runny nose. The chicken and the koftas were both super dry. And the naans were weird. Wholemeal and unleavened they were unpleasant and not as described in the menu.

To test our theory that the sweets were really the main event, we bought a couple for dessert. Surprise surprise they were significantly better than the mains. Just scrap the curries guys and stick with what you know.

title: Manapouri Cafe & Dairy
excerpt:
Fish and chips
Beef burger and chips

Manapouri Cafe & Dairy is the closest eatery to the popular Lake Manapouri jetty, so a certain amount of business is always going to come their way, and they know it. Consequently they haven’t put an awful lot of effort into their menu or cookery. The cook had a panicked vibe to her, bought us out another tables meals, and then when our meals arrived had forgotten the chips.

The highlight was the snapper which was fresh and well battered. It was served with mayo - why some places seem to think this is an acceptable substitute for tartare is beyond us. The burger wasn’t bad, just carelessly made, with a bland patty and the cheapest ingredients.

title: Pinch of Spice
excerpt:
Onion bhaji
Methi paneer
Chicken nilgiri
Plain naan
Cheese and garlic naan

We’ve only eaten out twice on Invercargill and by coincidence both have been Indian restaurants, for the record, Pinch of Spice is superior to Curry Guru the Malabar Kitchen in every way apart from the paneer.

Our curries were exciting and inventive. On multiple occasions we have ordered a “different” curry only to be given what is clearly a korma or masala under another name. So both of these were a pleasant surprise. Also pleasant was the chicken which was all tender meat with no mystery gristle. As we said, the paneer was weak. It was dry and had an unfortunate texture. The bhaji was the other weak link as it was floury in the centre and didn’t have enough sauce. The naans and rice both performed admirably.

title: ReBurger
excerpt:
Dirty Duke
BBQ Cheeseburg
Onion rings
Fried cauliflower

Giving ReBurger a rating was quite difficult for us. There is something inherently enjoyable about a burger and fried stuff, which sometimes inclines the Fee-Rex to give a place a higher rating than it perhaps deserves. However, the fact of the matter is that we’d both like to go back and eat another ReBurger, so that means that they fall into the 3 (good) category. Their fellow 3’s, Burgerfuel and Shake Out are superior, but ReBurger doesn’t belong in the same tier as McDonald’s and Carl’s Jr.

Both burgers were cut from the same, BBQ-ey cloth, the Dirty Duke had a thicker patty, some bacon, and some pickles, but they were otherwise quite similar. They were well constructed, with fresh buns, and well cooked meat patties. The aioli was much more noticeable in the BBQ Cheeseburg, and was sorely missed in the Dirty Duke.

The onion rings were hearty, real onion, and a good size, however they were desperately missing a dipping sauce. There was tomato sauce freely available, but that’s just not the right accompaniment for an onion ring. Perhaps if we had been given some aioli, we wouldn’t have noticed the oily taste in the batter so much. We really liked that they did fried cauliflower, and they were well sized pieces of actual cauliflower instead of just balls of cauliflower mush. They had been criminally over salted, but were really nice otherwise.

title: Cafe Eminem
excerpt:
Banana smoothie
Iced vanilla
Diablo pizza
Beef & lamb iskender

It’s so strange that there are two Turkish/Italian places to eat at in Palmerston North. Similar to Viva Cafe & Bar, Cafe Eminem is trying to be equal parts Turkish restaurant and Italian restaurant, and excelling at neither. Their decor was trying-to-be-fancy-while-not-spending-any-money chic, prominently featuring a fountain right in the middle of the restaurant that was not connected to any water.

Cafe Eminem was quiet when we got there, calm and ready to drop bombs, which they did in the form of two very disappointing beverages. The banana smoothie was clearly just crushed ice and ancient bananas, it was the colour of banana cake mix and about as thick. While we applaud the use of paper straws, and appreciate they at least gave wide bore straws, such straws just couldn’t handle the fortitude of these drinks. About half way through the drink the straws were completely collapsed. We tried tearing the straw, and turning it upside down, to no avail. The iced vanilla tasted like a watered down McDonald’s milkshake and was just as thick as the smoothie.

The iskender wasn’t too bad. Could have used more salad, and points off for not having any Turkish bread, but at least there was plenty of sauce, the rice was fresh and the meat wasn’t dry. The pizza was very heavy on the mozzarella, to the point of stringy absurdity at times. It was pretty flavourless, with the salami being beyond mild, and the onion was raw.

title: The Verdict
excerpt:
Banana smoothie
Beef stroganoff with rice
Beef burger and chips

The Verdict has been around since 1989 and has recently moved to a cursed building opposite Palmerston North City Council. Will they be able to survive atop the corpses of so many unfortunate cafe’s? While we weren’t impressed by The Verdict, there were plenty of people there who apparently were.

The banana smoothie committed two very serious offences. One was containing banana syrup. The other, even more heinous, was being insufficiently blended with large chunks of banana sitting at the bottom rendering the last inch undrinkable. It’s a shame because they had done some things right - the smoothie was large, and a great temperature and texture. But these two sins cannot be forgiven.

The stroganoff came from a bain-marie which had a fly hovering around it. Just in case it isn’t clear, flies on food = points off. It wasn’t really bad, but wasn’t good either. And where’s the sour cream?

The burger was tragically over-saladed. Three huge pieces of tomato. Four giant thick cut diagonal pieces of cucumber. And a full one inch tutu of lettuce protruding around the burger. While the salad was fresh, it was just way, way too much. It completely overshadowed the good elements of the burger, such as melty cheese, a fresh brioche bun, a moist tasty patty and some reasonable sauce. The chips had the flavour and texture of fairground cup-of-chips. It’s hard to describe exactly what was different about them, maybe the oil was old? Regardless, they weren’t great.

The verdict on The Verdict? Meh.

title: Flavour Bistro
excerpt:
Bruschetta
Panfried fish on Greek salad with potatoes
Coconut bubble tea with blueberry bubbles

What is Flavour? A restaurant that kind of thinks it’s fancy? A karaoke bar? A brunch spot? An ice cream parlour? A takeaway coffee joint?  Yes, yes, yes, yes, and yes. As is almost always the case, when somewhere tries to be all things to all people, it ends up being not much.

That said, the bruschetta was pretty good. It had giant pieces of tomato on it, which is normally a bad sign, but they pulled it off. The bread was thick, fresh and warm, the ratio of pesto, balsamic and feta was about right. The bubble tea was also pretty good, especially the exploding blueberry bubbles.

The fish was not great. The problem wasn’t necessarily the fish itself, but the sides. Where were the potatoes? There were literally two pieces of potato in that bowl. And the salad had way too many big whole olives.

Maybe if we were reviewing karaoke bars, or ice cream parlours, Flavour would have fared better. But as a dinner spot, while not a disaster, we wouldn’t go back again.

title: Pho Nem Hanoi Home Cooking
excerpt:
Tofu and shitake mushrooms with rice
Pork belly with rice
Honey and lemon tea

If you manage to impress The Fee-Rex with a plate of vegetables, you’re doing something right. While the carrot was overcooked, and the onion undercooked, the sauce was dynamite. The tofu and the rice were both good too.

The pork belly was a bit dry, and while it came with a little bit of a salad, the dish was a bit bare-bones overall. It did come with good rice, and another explosive sauce though.

The honey and lemon tea had a bit of marmalade at the bottom, and came in the world’s cutest cup with a little lid and an adorable teaspoon, we thoroughly enjoyed putting his wee hat back on him after each sip.

title: Nourish Cafe & Deli
excerpt:
Banana smoothie
Potato rosti with salad
Fried chicken with shoestring fries and salad
Melting moment

Being part of the unpopular food court is tough, but Nourish Cafe & Deli isn’t doing much to elevate their station.

The banana smoothie was a good temperature, but it was bland and far too thin. The rosti was exciting at first, it was nice to see something different in a cabinet, but it quickly became tiresome as the texture was quite claggy. The only flavour came from the sour cream and sweet chilli sauce that had been generously applied, and the side salad was fresh but boring. The exact same salad featured on the side of the fried chicken, which was fine, but the team at Nourish had clearly forgotten the secret herbs and spices. Shoestring fries were a nice change from the current thick cut paradigm, and there was plenty of mayo for dipping.

The highlight was the melting moment. It was fresh and crumbly, and was neither too sweet nor not sweet enough. The icing had a nice soft texture and there was just the right amount of it. We would happily eat this cookie again, which can’t be said for the rest of our meal.

title: Beyond Coffee
excerpt:
Fish tacos with salad
Fried mushrooms on toast
Passionfruit and orange smoothie

We were surprised to see a clientele of 80%+ grey tops when we walked in, but don’t let that paint a picture of one of those old lady cafes with the pie warmers and red plastic trays. The cabinet was actually quite interesting, although we elected to order off the menu.

The fish tacos were the weaker offering, the fish itself was just frozen hoki sticks, and while they had toasted the tacos and the chipotle mayo was pretty good, this dish was dragged down by its salad. The side salad was completely undressed, not even a dash of the most basic vinagrette. That’s bad enough until you realise that the salad was an add-on to the tacos and cost an additional $3.50. How very dare you!? An undressed salad is a crime, and being charged for it as a separate item is cause for the reintroduction of capital punishment. Seriously, fuck you, $3.50 for that? Not two blocks over, Empire Sports and Garden Bar Restaurant blows this place out of the water on value for money.

The mushrooms on toast were actually pretty good. We opted for fried over creamy and were not disappointed. The mushrooms were nicely garlicky, and came with two good thick slices of toast that had been slightly overdone but were still delicious. Extra points that the little butter packets were soft enough to spread, not the usual rock hard straight from the fridge ordeal.

The smoothie really should have been a juice. The flavours were weird, and the addition of orange juice meant that it kept separating into a foam layer and a juice layer. Not cool.

title: Leuven Belgium Beer Cafe
excerpt:
Venison meatballs
Cheese fondue with bread
Chips

Leuven is very Belgian, and they are taking their beer game seriously. This isn’t just some bar that’s serving Stella and calling it a day, there were literally dozens of different beers.

The meatballs were juicy and not too pungent or gamey, with a good tomato sauce. The fondue was very tasty, but absurdly stingy with the bread. It was annoying and confusing to run out of dipping materials one fifth of the way through the fondue. Thankfully we had a bowl of chips, which were thick cut and well suited to dipping. But you shouldn’t have to order an extra side to compensate for insufficient bread! And even with the chips Business Andy still ended up bringing down the tone of the establishment by finishing it off with a spoon.

title: Mekong Restaurant
excerpt:
Khao phad with tofu
Gaeng Panaeng with beef and rice

You may have noticed a pattern when Business Andy and The Fee-Rex visit Thai places. The Fee-Rex almost always orders a tofu pad thai, and Business Andy generally orders a Massaman Curry. Tonight we decided to branch out, and we were not rewarded.

The khao phad, which is fried rice with scant vegetables, was passable. The rice itself tasted a bit oily, but the tofu was top notch and it came with lime which was very welcome. The gaeng panaeng, which is supposed to be a rich peanut flavoured curry, was disgusting. To be more specific, the meat was revolting. Chewy, rubbery, gristly, fatty, bleugh. The sauce was bland. And the waitress waited until the curry was on the table before asking us if we wanted to order rice. At least the food came out quick, but that just meant we found out how expensive it was faster. Fifty dollars for a mediocre fried rice and a gross curry, not cool.

excerpt:

Mushrooms on toast
Banana smoothie

Common Ground Cafe puts in a solid performance in the brunch space, including fast service despite being busy. The menu is traditional but with a little bit of flair. Business Andy thought they were great, the Fee-Rex thought the dish had notes of feet, probably due to the parmesan. The weakest link was the banana smoothie, which was heavy on the yoghurt but light on overall banana flavour.

title: The Fat Farmer
excerpt:
Goats cheese with honey and hazlenuts
Polenta crumbed squid rings with mayo
Chicken bao buns
Pork bao buns
Gnocchi with pumpkin, sage and burnt butter
Chicken thigh with Israeli couscous
Tarte tartin with cream and mascarpone

Fat Farmer, you’ve done it again. At present, this is our favourite place to eat in Palmy. Tonight we had a few new dishes, and a few we’d had before. The goats cheese continues to be outstanding. We’ve had both bao buns before, and tonight we reaffirmed that the pork is indeed better than the chicken.

The squid rings, ooh lah lah. It was salty, but not too salty. And talk about tender. The gnocchi was scrumptious. The Fee-Rex loves to order gnocchi then say that it’s gross - but not tonight! Pan fried to perfection, the pumpkin a perfect accompaniment, and the burnt butter sauce was extra. The chicken was the weakest link. It wasn’t bad, but when surrounded by these giants of deliciousness, it paled in comparison. The tarte tartin was ginormous and bloody nice. We were surprised by how large it was and took half home. We didn’t spring for the ice cream on the side, and this was a mistake. As always, the cocktails were also great.

Bookings still essential.
